notes: On 12 September 2020, people protested near Rolofshagen against the expansion of wind energy plants. The protest was organized by an AfD politician.

On 10 November 2020, 16 teachers protested in Auxerre to denounce the government's management of the coronavirus health crisis. They denounced a lack of means and space so that the classes could safely take place. They called for splitting up classes into small groups in middle schools. They also called for more financial, material, and human resources. They also denounced what they perceive as disdain from the government.
On 14 August 2020, hundreds of citizens gathered in front of the Royal Palace of La Almudaina in Mallorca [coded to Palma de Mallorca] to protest against the Monarchy.

On 28 July 2023, Kvinnostrejk movement activists demonstrated in Ostersund, Jamtland, in support of women's rights and to oppose violence against women. The county officials participated in the event, among others.
On 19 January 2020, around 200 people protested in Arad, demanding the closing of the city's north-west belt road.

On 21 February 2020, about 250 activists gathered in Trnava, commemorating a murdered journalist and his fiancee and demanding proper investigation of the crime as well as alleged close ties between the government and criminal structures. The event was organized by the movement For Decent Slovakia.

On 4 May 2024, at the call of the Xunta pola Defensa de la Llingua Asturiana (XDLA), people, including the minister of culture (PSOE) and other PSOE representatives as well as IU and Podemos deputies, protested in Oviedo (Asturias) to claim the official status of the Asturian language.

On 8 February 2025, around 2,000 teachers, called by the Board of Teaching Staff, protested in Santander (Cantabria) to reject the government's latest salary adjustment proposal, which they deemed insufficient. Protesters criticized the regional government's offer of a 90-euro increase in three installments, while also condemning proposed conditions tying salary increases to attendance, arguing it unfairly penalized teachers on medical leave.

On 10 November 2023, 4,000 people held a protest in front of the PSOE headquarters in Madrid - Chamberi (Madrid) after the PSOE closed an investiture agreement with pro-independence parties that includes an amnesty law. The protesters demanded the resignation of President Pedro Sanchez.

On 18 November 2023, at the call of the CGT and the BDS, around 500 people staged a protest action on Republique Street in Orleans (Centre-Val de Loire) to demand a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas, show support for the Palestinian people and condemn the Israeli military campaign in and around Gaza.
On 28 September 2020, an unknown number of people staged a protest in front of the Elia headquarters in Ecaussinnes to denounce the construction of a high voltage line in their neighborhood.

On 10 January 2024, 8 Last Generation activists protested in Bremen (Bremen) with a sit-in and by gluing themselves and some toy tractors onto the road. They protested against the climate policies of the federal government, for more social equality in the climate crisis and to denounce 'double standards' in the coverage of their protests and their climate demands, and those of the farmers, many of whom were protesting against planned cuts to agricultural subsidies at the time of reporting. Police forces intervened, removed the protesters from the road and brought them to the police station.

On 18 February 2024, around 80 people, including representatives of ADFC, BUND, NABU, 'Climate decision Duisburg' (Klimaentscheid Duisburg), The Left, The Greens and Volt Europa, participated in a cycling protest in Duisburg (Nordrhein-Westfalen) against the tree policies of the city administration and the felling of trees. They argued that although preserving the trees was costly, it was worth it from a climate perspective.

On 9 March 2021, about 1000 sports and fitness workers took part in a sit-in in Del Popolo square in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to protest against the ongoing closure of some sports facilities and fitness centers across the country due to the coronavirus emergency and demand their reopening at once. During the demonstration, a Lega Senator sought to address protesters in sign of support, yet was reportedly booed and insulted, and consequently escorted out of the square. There was no report of violence.
On 26 February 2022, several thousand Polish and Ukrainian activists gathered for a rally in Warsaw, protesting against the Russian military aggression against Ukraine.

On 31 January 2024, around 20 farmers and other entrepreneurs with about 25 tractors and trucks protested on road B90 near Bad Lobenstein (Thuringen) and blocked the A9 highway ramp. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement against several agricultural policies of the federal government, including planned agricultural subsidy cuts.

On 29 September 2022, overnight, people gathered for a protest organized by the Boars Radicalized Collective, and ransacked the golf course of Saint-Cloud in Rueil-Malmaison (Nanterre, Hauts-de-Seine, Ile-de-France) against the 'leisure's of the rich' and the pension reform.
On 29 September 2020, an unknown number of people staged a protest on Het Plein in Den Haag against the coronavirus protection laws of the Dutch government.

On 23 June 2021, local environmental activists and FIOM CGIL, FIM CISL and UILM (UIL) trade unionists gathered outside the Prefecture in Taranto (Taranto, Puglia) to call for the shutdown of the Ex Ilva steel factory's blast furnaces due to pollution concerns.

On 19 March 2021, activists gathered in Ziar nad Hronom and demonstratively painted a local house with slogans demanding better protection of the climate. Due to COVID-19 mandatory rules, traditional marches and demonstrations were not allowed, and they explicitly used this form of protest instead.
On 3 July 2021, people protested in Kiel for climate justice.

On 9 February 2023, around 200 workers of the Huesca City Council held a protest in Huesca (Aragon) against the loss of the seniority supplement, which had been paid for over 30 years and received by more than 300 municipal employees.
On 16 April 2021, PD members, as well as one PD MP, held a rally in Ndroq, denouncing the Rama government, promising reforms, and calling on people to vote.

On 9 January 2021, dozens of persons, including parents of students, physicians, and teachers, gathered in Bourges. They denounced the coronavirus-related obligation for children under eleven years old to wear masks at school and its consequences on their health.
On 26 June 2018, more than one hundred people protested in Cluj-Napoca demanding the resignation of PM Viorica Dancila and PSD leader Liviu Dragnea.
On 11 June 2021, health workers protested in front of the hospital of A Coruna, demanding the resignation of the hospital nursing management.
On 15 August 2020, activists of Platform for Progress protested in Banja Luka, Bosnia and Herzegovina, against political corruption and demanding a 'ministry of diaspora' be formed.

On 17 December 2021, at the call of CGT and CFDT, around 30 Departmental Center for Children and Families (CDEF) employees gathered outside the Departmental Council in Saint-Brieuc (Bretagne) to protest against the restructuring of their workplace.

On 22 September 2023, Fridays For Future activists demonstrated in Oskarshamn, Kalmar, to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change. The demonstration was part of the global climate action held on 22 September.

On 25 May 2023, civil servants of the administration of justice held a protest in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria (Las Palmas, Canarias) as part of their ongoing protest to demand a dignified work, a salary raise, and against the Organic Law of Organizational Efficiency (LOEO). The protest was summoned by STAJ, CSIF, UGT, and CCOO.

On 23 February 2021, around 70 Antifa activists protested with a sit-in in Vienna - Alsergrund in front of a police detention centre against the deportation of refugees to Afghanistan. Several activists climbed and chained themselves to a steel framework, they had to be rescued by the fire department and the police. Later that day, around 150 to 200 people gathered again to protest against deportations to Afghanistan.

On 28 March 2023, 25,000 people, including students, took to the streets of Nice to demonstrate. Earlier that day, people gathered and blocked traffic in the PAL industrial area of the Saint-Isidore neighborhood of the city. The events were part of a tenth national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FAGE, FIDL, and MNL) to oppose the passing of a pension reform bill by means of Article 49.3 of the constitution by the government, and call for the withdrawal of the bill.
On 13 August 2018, 2018: Citizens from Karlovo and municipal villages protested against the closing of the obstetric-gynecological department of the hospital in Karlovo due to the lack of staff.

On 14 October 2020, peddlers gathered outside the Sicily region headquarters in Catania to protest against the local measures to stop the spread of coronavirus. They claim that the measures are too strict and they are worsening the economic crisis in their sector.
On 9 September 2021, local residents gathered in Sevilla to protest against Endesa electric utility company power cuts in several areas.

On 17 November 2024, at the call of FNSEA and JA, farmers drove around 20 tractors and 30 cars at a slow pace to protest from several localities to the Airbase in Velizy-Villacoublay (Ile-de-France), causing severe traffic disruption. The event was part of a nationwide demonstration movement by French farmers opposing the EU-Mercosur trade deal and condemning delays in agricultural reforms promised by the previous government following the winter 2023-2024 farmers' demonstrations.

On 20 March 2021, several dozen protesters gathered in Cathedral Square in central Vilnius to demonstrate against coronavirus restrictions, especially compulsory wearing of face masks. An MP from the opposition Freedom and Justice party was present at the event. The rally was reportedly part of an international movement, which organized protests against coronavirus restrictions on this day in over 50 countries.

Around 28 November 2022 (as reported), people, including many women, gathered for a protest in front of the Tour de Paris in Villeneuve-sur-Lot, on the occasion of the International Day against violence against women.

On 19 March 2021, more than 200 Fridays for Future and Seebruecke activists protested in Erfurt for more climate action. The protest was part of a Global Climate Strike with the motto 'No More Empty Promises'.

On 16 February 2021, parents, teachers, and elected officials, protested in Pont-Audemer in front of a school against budget cuts concerning resources allocated for the start of the 2021 school year, causing a class closure.

On 23 September 2021, between 70 and 80 teachers demonstrated in Laval, at the call of unions (CGT, FO, Sud, SNES-FSU). They denounced their working conditions and demanded for an increase of their emoluments.

On 20 July 2024, hundreds of residents gathered outside the Riverside building on Charlottes Quay in Limerick (Limerick City and County) against the plans to use the building to accommodate asylum seekers and refugees. The demonstration was peaceful, with the crowd singing Ole Ole Ole. Limerick Says No organized the protest.
On 12 September 2022, around 600 people demonstrated in Kothen for peace in Ukraine and against 'state paternalism' concerning health and other matters.
On 21 October 2020, around 400 employees of the city administration, of BS Energy and job centers protested in Braunschweig for higher salaries. The protest was organized by Ver.di.

On 12 October 2020, 18 police officers demonstrated in front of the police station in Concarneau, at the call of the SGP union. They denounced the riot against the police station of Champigny-sur-Marne days before and denounced the violence and threats that they experience.

On 23 January 2021, dozens of people protested in front of the Russian Embassy in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) for the release of opposition leader Aleksei Navalny. There were also people marching against Navalny nearby, carrying signs reading 'Navalny is criminal'.

On 14 February 2021, people working in the cultural industry protested in Braunschweig to draw attention to their difficult situation during the coronavirus pandemic. Members of The Right, NPD and JN participated in the protest.

On 17 April 2023, thousands of activists gathered for a rally and a march in Prague, demanding immediate resignation of the government over alleged failures related to the energy crisis and inflation. They also criticized allegedly too extensive assistance to Ukraine during the ongoing war at the expense of the Czech citizens and some of them declared support to the Russian cause. Several dozens of them decided to stay overnight. The event was organized by the newly established PRO party and a MP of SPD actively participated too. Counter-protesters gathered nearby, criticizing the protest against the government over its alleged pro-Russian dimension and declared their support to Ukraine. Ukrainian activists also participated.
On 26 May 2019, approximately 70 people protested outside the PSD regional office in Sibiu against the PSD-ALDE government.
On 27 December 2022, workers of the Chinese copper manufacturing company protested in Bor, demanding the annulment of the work regulations and the signing of a collective agreement.

On 28 May 2021, tens of locals protested outside the poultry processing factory in Floreni, demanding that the company pay for its pollution and that it connect to the sewage system. Employees of the factory came out and pushed some protesters, but the police intervened to prevent the clashes.
On 20 August 2019, civil society and members of patriotic organizations held a protest at the memorial located in honor of the 251 Turkish citizens killed during the 2016 coup in Turkey.

On 7 April 2021, two well-known anti-distance learning student activists and students' parents affiliated with the Priority to School committee gathered in Castello square, in front of the Piemonte Region headquarters, in Torino (Torino, Piemonte) to protest against the recourse to distance learning amidst the coronavirus emergency.

On 22 February 2025, under the motto 'Together for Tolerance and Humanity - Stop the Far-Right Shift', at least 300 people gathered in Wiesbaden (Hessen) to protest against far-right ideologies. The event was part of a nationwide protest movement focused on defending democracy ahead of the 2025 federal elections.
On 3 November 2021, police officers protested in A Coruna (Galicia), demanding better working conditions and a salary increase. Protesters jeered against the councillor.
On 12 May 2021, health workers protested at a hospital in Crailsheim for better working conditions in the health sector on the occasion of International Nurses Day.
On 29 May 2021, dozens of residents of the city demonstrated in Saulnes. They denounced industrial noise pollution due to the destruction of a building and farming.

On 25 June 2020, people staged a protest in Ragusa (Ragusa, Sicily) against the guidelines proposed by the Italian Minister of Education for the reopening of Italian schools in September following the coronavirus lockdown. Protesters gathered at the call of the Priority to School committee. Trade union Flc Cgil was present.
On 20 February 2020, over 300 persons gathered in Nantes. They protested in memory of a victim of police brutality and to demand justice.

On 6 March 2024, the Transfeminist University Assembly (AUT - Assemblea Universitaria Transfemminista) occupied the psychology department at the university in Padova (Veneto) to protest against cases of harassment against female and transgender students and staffers happening within the university. Protesters asked for an anti-violence center within the university and for the introduction of transfeminist education into the curriculum.
On 22 May 2019, in Bukovica, Montenegro, residents protested over the construction of a mini hydro powerplant.

On 29 September 2020, around 20 workers of Alestis Aerospace company enclosed themselves at the companies' headquarters in Sevilla to protest against dismissal proceedings affecting around 585 employees. Representatives of the General Union of Workers (UGT) and Workers Commissions (CCOO) participated in the protest.

On 14 October 2020, teachers with a temporary contract gathered in Rome to protest against the decision to set the national exam for a permanent position at the end of the month. They claim that taking the exam during the coronavirus emergency is risky for the exam candidates and unfair for the candidates who can't make it because they have to quarantine at home. They also asked for a permanent job contract after years of temporary employment. The demonstration was supported by Priority to School and the labor unions CGIL, CISL, UIL, SNALS and Gilda.
On 14 April 2023, an unknown number of people occupied a tollgate area in Saint-Selve, allowing drivers to pass freely, in opposition to the passing of the pension reform bill.

On 31 March 2020, five people from Nigeria staged a protest at the CAS (Emergency Reception Center) in San Baronto (Pistoia, Toscana) where they are hosted, claiming that the management was not fair with them. Protesters laid on the ground preventing people working at the center from leaving.
On 10 December 2022, citizens, mostly transgender collective members and other LGBT groups, held a protest in Arrecife (Las Palmas, Canarias) against the amendments to the Trans Law made by the PSOE.
On 3 December 2023, farmers blocked the road with their tractors in Zupanja, voicing their dissatisfaction with the lack of governmental measures to assist them in dealing with swine influenza.

On 11 April 2021, over 600 persons gathered in Quimperle. They denounced the national health state of emergency amid the coronavirus pandemic, the obligation to wear masks in public places and the vaccination campaign.
On 28 January 2022, Fridays for Future activists demonstrated in Kalmar to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.
On 26 July 2020, around 1,500 motorbikers protested in Freiburg im Breisgau against a planned driving ban for motorbikes to reduce traffic noise.

On 2 June 2023, residents of Kresna protested against the expansion of the Struma highway that would go through the Kresna Gorge. They claim the highway will damage the natural park around the gorge and that locals do not agree with the expansion.

On 28 October 2020, an unspecified number of people, most of them local shop, restaurant and bar owners, gathered in Salotto square in Pescara to protest against the restrictions to their activity introduced by decree of the President of the Council of Ministers amidst a second wave of coronavirus infections. The protest, which also saw the participation of the city's mayor and some of his advisors, was supported by CONFCOMMERCIO, Confartigianato, CNA and Confesercenti.

On 14 February 2021, about 300 demonstrators - organized on social media without an official organizer of the rally - gathered at Syntagma square in Athens - Central Athens against the government's coronavirus lockdown measures. Demonstrators clashed with riot police after they attempted to occupy the road blocking traffic in front of parliament.

On 15 June 2023, around 40 retirees staged a protest in front of the Prefecture in Mont-de-Marsan to demand a raise of their pensions in the face of inflation. The protest was an initiative of the Group of 9, a coalition formed by CGT, FO, CFTC, CFE-CGC, FSU, SUD, Federation Generale des Retraites de la Fonction publique (FGR-FP), LSR, Ensemble et Solidaires.

On 28 September 2024, pro-Palestinian demonstrators from Eindhoven4Palestine marched through the city center of Eindhoven (Noord-Brabant), starting at the 18 Septemberplein, to protest what they called a genocide in Palestine, and to demand an end to the Israeli occupation and Dutch complicity herein. The march included speeches and a route through the Kleine Berg and followed smaller protests earlier in the week at the technical university of Eindhoven.
On 5 February 2018, around 40 people protested outside the PSD regional office in Sibiu, raising concern about the penal code modifications on corruption, and the judicial system.

On 12 January 2023, between 800 (according to the Government Delegation) and 3,000 (according to the organizers) taxi drivers held a protest in Madrid - Tetuan (Madrid) against the transport regulations that the regional government will implement.

On 4 February 2022, in the morning, a few dozen people gathered, at the call of 'Verona For Freedom' ('Verona per la verita') committee, outside the Tribunal of Verona (Verona, Veneto) to protest against coronavirus 'green pass' restrictions and denounce the encroachment on individual freedoms allegedly entailed.

On 15 May 2025, at 7:30 pm, at the call of the Brest branch of the Collective for a Just and Lasting Peace in the Middle East (Collectif brestois pour une paix juste et durable au Proche-Orient), between 90 and 150 people gathered in Brest (Bretagne) to call for peace in Gaza and express support for the Palestinian people. Protesters held portraits of 20 Palestinian victims. The event was part of a national initiative organized and called by the White Coats for Gaza collective (Blouses Blanches pour Gaza).

On 17 February 2024, at the call of 'Action Alliance Meckenbeuren' (Aktionsbundnis Meckenbeuren) consisting of city council members, a retired chaplain and a cycling club, 300 to 400 people, including Grannies Against the Right, the mayor, a former Church community council, members of the Youth Council, and representatives of the 'Meeting Place' (Begegnungstreff), participated in a protest in Meckenbeuren (Baden-Wurttemberg) for diversity, democracy, tolerance, respect and humanity. The protest was organized following reports about a secret meeting between AfD members and far-right activists in Potsdam in November 2023, during which remigration plans were discussed.

On 27 January 2024, around 2,200 people took part in a protest in Rendsburg (Schleswig-Holstein) against right-wing extremism. The protest was prompted by concerns over a secret meeting between AfD representatives and other far-right activists, discussing mass deportations of individuals with German citizenship and migrant background, leading to a heightened awareness and mobilization against far-right ideas in various cities.

On 14 March 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of XR and Quit with Coal, an unspecified number of people gathered at the Uniper coal plant on Maasvlakte Rotterdam (Zuid-Holland), blocking traffic, to protest the environmental harm caused by fossil subsidies. The demonstration criticized their foreign ownership, imports of non-local resources, and export-driven production. The action was part of Operation Storm, involving multiple actions over three days targeting companies receiving fossil fuel subsidies.
On 20 September 2022, ORP activists gathered for a rally in Gdynia, protesting against alleged politicization of courts in Poland.
On 31 January 2025, farmers continued their mobilizations over rising production costs among other issues. Farmers rolled out 25 tractors at the city entrance of Kilkis.
Around 4 February 2023 (as reported), people gathered for a protest at their school in Loures-Barousse, against the closure of a class in their school.

On 6 April 2023, at 2:30 pm, people including GGT members gathered at the train station in La Rochelle and headed towards the city center via the old port before returning to the station. The event was part of an eleventh national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FAGE, FIDL, and MNL) to oppose the passing of a pension reform bill by means of Article 49.3 of the constitution by the government, and call for the withdrawal of the bill.

On 21 December 2024, Sudanese citizens organized a demonstration in front of the European Union headquarters in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to show support for the Sudanese Armed Forces, holding up a sign saying 'RSF is a terrorist militia'.
On 1 March 2019, in Rekovac, Serbia citizens held a protest against the regime of Aleksandar Vucic. This protest was a part of a series of protests happening throughout the country for several weeks.
On 16 May 2020, around 300 yellow vests demonstrated in Lyon. The reason of the protest was not specified. Many wore masks, in compliance with measures implemented to prevent the spread of COVID-19.

On 4 March 2025, civil servants, called by the Interunion Platform against the healthcare collapse (Plataforma Intersindical frente al colapso sanitario), held a protest in Melilla (Melilla) to demand the continuation of their healthcare coverage under the Muface system. Protesters urged the government to reach an agreement ensuring uninterrupted access to healthcare services, condemning delays in treatments and diagnostic procedures. They criticized the uncertainty surrounding the healthcare agreement and denounced the government and insurers for prioritizing financial interests over patient care.

On 24 July 2020, about 70 employees of the airline easyJet, organized by Unite the Union, staged a protest outside of London Stansted airport in Stansted Mountfitchet in response to the company's announcement that thousands of jobs will be made redundant amidst the coronavirus pandemic.
On 7 April 2019, in Stari Grad area in Serbian capital Belgrade, approximately 20 residents gathered to protest the announced reconstruction of the park by planting trees.
On 9 January 2024, teachers, including SNES-FSU affiliates, gathered outside the Bristol school in Nice (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to demand more staff and more security.
On 8 November 2024, at the call of UIL, workers, pensioners, and students staged a protest in Potenza (Basilicata) to protest against job insecurity and youth unemployment.

On 12 October 2020, at least 7 Greenpeace and Fridays for Future activists, as well as researchers, scientists, and actors, protested outside the Karmelita government building in Budapest I, demanding the Hungarian government to adopt the reduction of CO2 by at least 65% by 2030 at EU level.
On 12 January 2020, thousands marched in Herceg Novi, Montenegro, against the Religious Freedom Law that was recently passed. The law is primarily opposed by (Serbian) Orthodox Christians.

On 6 September 2020, protesters against a regulation obliging children to wear face masks when they return to school as part of the government's coronavirus measures rallied in Arta. The protesters, who were holding Greek national flags and comprised of a diverse crowd including parents, members of the anti-vaccine movement and Orthodox Christian religious groups organised in social media, stamped on face masks and burned them, while chanting slogans against the Prime Minister.

On 26 November 2021, University of Bari students gathered, at the call of the LINK union, in Cesare Battisti square in Bari (Bari, Puglia) to call for their university to change its fee regulations, denouncing the increase in study-related costs.

On 23 January 2023, public sector workers and Ver.di members demonstrated in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg) in front of the Finance Authority, shortly before the start of federal and local government wage negotiations, to call for better pay.

On 2 December 2023, striking delivery riders gathered in Auxerre (Bourgogne-Franche-Comte). The event was part of a nationwide strike of delivery drivers called by CGT Transports, SUD-Commerces, and Union-Independants (CFDT) to demand better working conditions and a pay rise.

Around 18 June 2020, an unknown number of health workers staged a protest at the Millegem retirement home in Ranst in the context of a national action day against the underfunding of the health sector. The action was organized by ACV Puls.

On 24 September 2024, at the call of FNADEPA - National Federation of Associations of Directors of Establishments and Services for the Elderly (Federation Nationale des Associations de Directeurs d'Etablissements & Services pour Personnes Agees), residents, their families, and employees gathered outside the Abbaye elderly home (EHPAD) in Grenoble (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes). The event was part of a nationwide strike and demonstration movement of elderly home residents and employees called by FNAAFP - Federation of Directors of Establishments for the Elderly (Federation des Directeurs d'Etablissements pour Personnes Agees) and named 'The Elderly Deserve More' (Les Vieux Meritent Mieux) to demand more financial funding and better services in their sector.
On 28 March 2023, over 50 La Vaguada residents held a protest in Zamora (Castilla y Leon) against the car parking that is being built in the area to accommodate some 80 vehicles.

On 3 December 2022, more than one hundred people carried out a demonstration in Folgueroles (Cataluna) repudiating the late opening of a Christmas festival that was planned to start on November 4. The Town Hall had already denied the permits for this initiative arguing that the documentation requested for the market were received late. Private organizers stated that they will file an appeal against the decision.

On 7 December 2020, about 20 activists affiliated to the movement Million Moments for Democracy gathered for a rally in Karlovy Vary, protesting against alleged harmful pressure against the media of public service from politicians. They demanded preservation of independence especially of the national TV station Czech Television.

On 31 October 2022, around 600 people, including farmers with 22 tractors, demonstrated in Torgau against high energy costs, and inflation, which they blame on the war in Ukraine and coronavirus-related measures. They demonstrated from the market square through the old town.

On 9 January 2024, parents and members of teacher's associations staged a protest outside 2 schools for children with autism in Pylaia, demanding a solution after the school buildings were deemed unsafe.

On 2 February 2024, teachers gathered outside the rectorate in Ajaccio (Corse). The event was part of a national strike and protest movement called by CGT, FO, SUD Education, UNSA Education, SNUIPP-FSU, SNALC, and SGEN CFDT to demand higher wages and better working conditions at public schools after Minister of Education Amelie Oudea-Castera issued comments they deemed disrespectful to teachers.

On 13 February 2022, 2,000 to 3,000 people staged a protest in Den Haag against the coronavirus regulations of the Dutch government. The protest was an initiative of Nederland in Verzet. Also a trucker protest at the A12 highway in Den Haag was reported, after trucks were forbidden to join the protesters in the city center by the municipal authorities.

On 5 May 2024, around 100 people took to the streets to demonstrate in Pau (Nouvelle-Aquitaine). The event was part of a nationwide demonstration day called by 800 organizations, including LGBTQ+ collectives, feminist associations, PS, MFPF, AUP, The Ecologists, SUD, NPA, NT, SOS Homophobie, and LFI, to condemn transphobia after the publication of a Senate LR-championed bill on transidentity and the promotion of the book 'Transmania', both of which the protesters deemed transphobic.

On 24 January 2022, campaigners belonging to Stop HS2 and HS2 Rebellion (associated with Extinction Rebellion) demonstrated with banners and a prop elephant called Nelly at Euston station in London - Camden as part of a full day of action against the expansion of the HS2 infrastructure project.

On 18 November 2022, residents of Divjake protested against plans by the municipality to install a toll booth at the entrance of the Divjake-Karavasta national park. They claim the toll booth will make it more expensive for local residents to visit the national park, as well as significantly reduce income for the small businesses operating inside the park since Divjake is not a major tourism center in Albania and already gets limited income.

On 9 June 2022, metal workers, along with UGT, CIG, and CCOO members, have participated in the seventh day of the strike in the region of Ferrol (A Coruna, Galicia), with mobilizations and informational pickets, demanding a 'decent' agreement and with demands for wages and also for subrogation of employees.
On 8 September 2024, Extinction Rebellion activists staged a sit-in protest at the Copenhagen Airport in Kastrup, Hovedstaden, calling for a ban on private jets and opposing the aviation industry.
On 29 January 2025, at the call of CGT, striking firefighters gathered for a picket line in Aix-en-Provence (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to demand more staff and better working conditions.

On 23 September 2022, members of environmental groups Fridays For Future, Oikopolis, Eterotopia and Animal Save rallied and marched in Thessaloniki over climate change carrying placards and banners. They also protested against the use of fossil fuels.

On 27 June 2023, around 200 RTE employees (Irish public service broadcaster) held a protest outside offices in Donegal (Donegal) after the revelation of the payments controversy to Irish broadcaster Ryan Tubridy. The protest was organized by the National Union of Journalists and SIPTU. The event was part of a national day of action.

On 23 May 2023, climate activists from Just Stop Oil, Fossil Free, and Money Rebellion protested at Shell's annual shareholder meeting in ExCel London - Newham. Protesters tried to disrupt the meeting, and security forces repeatedly escorted them out.

On 23 February 2025, more than 50 people participated in the 'Light a candle for the fallen defenders of Ukrainian freedom' campaign in Kaunas, Lithuania, in support of Ukraine. The event was held to mark the third anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and the ongoing war that followed.
On 23 April 2021, environmental activists protested in Hofors to oppose clear-cutting of forests in various areas in Sweden.
On 15 February 2019, in Arandelovac, Serbia, citizens held an anti-government protest, part of a series of protests happening throughout the country for several consecutive weeks.

On 5 October 2024, more than 200 people gathered in Brindisi (Puglia) to commemorate a 20-year-old who died in a road accident and call for safe roads and stricter speed limits. Mayor Giuseppe Marchionna (Civic List), Councilor for Public Works Cosimo Elmo (FI), and representatives of the 'Italian Association of Relatives of Road Victims' (Aifvs) partook in the demonstration.

On 23 September 2024, citizens organized by the informal group 'Mirijevo Green and Healthy' protested in Mirijevo in Belgrade - Zvezdara against the planned cutting of 66 hectares of forest near the 'Bajdina' area for to the construction of residential and commercial buildings. The protest was interrupted by individuals claiming to be owners of the plot, who attempted to interrupt the demonstration. The police we called to re-established order and identified those who attempted to interrupt the gathering

On 28 September 2021, students occupied their schools in Fthiotida [coded to Lamia] demanding increased coronavirus safety measures, more teaching and cleaning staff hirings in schools, no coronavirus tests for unvaccinated students, and they protested against the introduction of a minimum passing grade at university entrance exams among other issues. This was part of a student mobilization occupying 130 schools across the country called by the Coordinating Committee of Students.

On 10 February 2021, dozens of workers of ski resorts of the Aragonese Pyrenees gathered in Huesca, demanding that the regional government provide direct aids to their labor sector. Protesters complained about their difficult economic conditions caused by the coronavirus restrictions. The Sos Pyrenees Benasque Valley called the protest.

On 2 February 2025, citizens and students gathered in Trstenik to show support for students who are occupying their faculties, demanding accountability for the loss of 15 lives after a concrete canopy at Novi Sad's railway station collapsed, attributing the tragic event to corruption. Protesters also observed 15 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign, with an aim to honor the 15 victims and demand accountability for their loss of life.

On 22 May 2024, people, called by Omnium Cultural, held a protest in front of the regional Court in Hospitalet de Llobregat (Cataluna) in support of the pro-independence Catalan activists currently being investigated for terrorism after taking part in Democratic Tsunami demonstrations.

On 23 February 2023, about 30 residents of the Lavino neighborhood in Anzola dell'Emilia gathered in Bologna (Bologna, Emilia-Romagna), outside the oratory San Filippo Neri where a conference on land consumption sponsored by the city of Bologna was being held, to protest against the construction of a supermarket in a green area in Lavino. Legambiente representatives were among the demonstrators against the project which, in addition to damage pristine soil, is likely to soar pollution levels due to envisaged traffic increase.
On 30 January 2023, people demonstrated in Neubrandenburg against the war in Ukraine and its consequence on the government's energy policy. They also denounced inflation.

On 1 April 2025, 15 temporary security workers staged a protest at the San Francesco d'Assisi Airport in Perugia (Umbria) against the outsourcing of security services by Sase, the airport management company, due to a reduction in wages due to the new company's application of a less favorable contract.

On 23 June 2024, between 250 and 300 people demonstrated in Chambery (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes). The event was part of a nationwide wave of demonstrations called by CFDT, CGT, UNSA, SUD, and FSU, as well as more than 200 feminist organizations such as MFPF, NT, and Oxfam, condemning far-right ideology, which the demonstrators deemed dangerous to women's rights. The event took place after the National Rally (RN) came first in the European elections in France and President Emmanuel Macron announced the dissolution of the National Assembly on 9 June 2024, prompting snap legislative elections, raising fears of a government led by the far-right party.
On 7 October 2021, an unknown number of AG Insurance workers staged a protest at the company's headquarters in Antwerpen to denounce high work pressure due to telework.

On 26 October 2022, Allianz Partner workers staged a demonstration, for the second consecutive day, in the Citylife neighborhood in Milano - Municipio 8 (Milano, Lombardia) to request that the presence in the company of the USB trade union, which workers have recently joined, be officially recognized.
On 28 October 2020, several hundred activists, mostly women, gathered for a rally in Mogilno, protesting against restrictions of abortions in Poland. The event was coordinated by the Women's Strike.

On 12 October 2024, between around 3,000 and 5,000 Pro-Palestinian activists and campaigners marched from the Pyramid of Caius Cestius to Vittorio Square in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to demand a stop to the bombing of Gaza by Israeli armed forces. Protesters waved Palestinian, Lebanese and peace flags, and held a banner with the words 'With Hamas until victory' and 'Stop the genocide of the Palestinian population, stop the massacre in Lebanon', while chanting anti-Israel slogans. Members of ANPI, the Palestinian community, USB, UDU, CR and PCI took part in the event.

On 11 February 2023, between 6,000 (according to the authorities) and 15,000 (according to the unions) people staged a protest march in Morlaix. The event was part of a fourth national and cross-sector day of strike and protest called by CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform.

On 1 April 2020, around 20 migrant workers and agricultural day laborers living in a tent camp in San Ferdinando (Reggio di Calabria, Calabria) staged a rally after the right-wing regional councilor for Security tried to establish a canteen service instead of meeting the migrants' request for help to get food that they could cook. Rioters damaged the cage located at the entrance of the tent camp where entrances and exits are recorded.

On 5 December 2020, between 600 and 1,000 persons demonstrated in Valence. They called for the removal of article 24 of the 'comprehensive security' bill and denounced its potential infringement of the principle of freedom of information, especially on reporting on police brutality. The article criminalizes disseminating images with personal identifiers of a police or military officer, with the aim of affecting his or her physical or psychological integrity.

On 18 March 2023, around 400 people gathered in Gueret to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. Representatives of the CGT and CDFT unions and PS and NPA parties were present. Also teachers and parents were present to denounce the school reforms in the Creuse region.
On 16 May 2020, around 60 people, including Green Youth activists, protested in Heidelberg under the motto 'Together through the crisis' in connection wtih the coronavirus pandemic.
On 22 February 2025, more than 2,000 people, including farmers and fishers, gathered in Redon (Bretagne) to protest against the use of pesticides and to demand the preservation of water resources.
On 29 October 2020, activists, mostly women, gathered for a rally in Miedzyrzecz protesting against restrictions of abortions in Poland. The event was coordinated by the Women's Strike.

On Mar. 5, 2018: Environmental activists held a rally in Tirana in protest against various construction works in protected and tourist areas. Protesters said they were trying to stop the irreversible destruction of Albanian nature by private firms that violate laws and corrupt judges who helped them.

On 21 October 2023, around 200 people participated in a protest on Luisenplatz in Neuwied (Rheinland-Pfalz) organized by 'Bundnis fur Demokratie und Toleranz' (Alliance for Democracy and Tolerance) under the motto 'Neuwied stands up against the Right' to set a sign against the right and the AfD in particular.

On 9 November 2020, people gathered for a 'Walk for Freedom' in Leipzig to protest against the coronavirus protection measures. Around 1,000 people gathered for a counter-protest and commemorated the victims of the Night of Broken Glass (Reichsprogromnacht) 82 years ago.

On 13 January 2024, tens of Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot activists and conscientious objectors rallied at Ledras crossing point in Nicosia, protesting for a demilitarized Cyprus and expressing their solidarity with a Turkish Cypriot conscientious objector, who was refusing to enlist in the army. The protesters also decried the hostile approach taken by the authorities on both sides of the island. Representatives of the platform Conscientious Objectors Cyprus, AKEL, Volt Cyprus, the movement AFOA (anti-capitalism, ecology, feminism, autonomy), and the multi-communal youth initiative Hade, participated in the protest.

On 1 May 2021, citizens protested in Palencia, including CCOO and UGT, calling for a fair way out from the health and economic crisis caused by the coronavirus pandemic on International Labor Day. They demanded the government to assign priority to the social agenda.

On 25 November 2023, at the call of CISL, people including pensioners, young people and women gathered in Sant'Apostoli square in Rome - City Center (Lazio, Roma) to ask the Government to improve the financial maneuver and build a new social pact. CISL general secretary and regional secretaries were present.

On 7 June 2024, people gathered outside the Donegal County Council offices in Letterkenny (Donegal) to highlight that 40% of childcare services in the county are affected by defective concrete. Protesters carried signs that read 'Save Our Playgroup' and 'Where Will We Go?'.
On 28 June 2022, citizens held a demonstration for LGBT rights in Girona (Cataluna), and demanded a determined and constant fight against hate crimes and aggressions against the collective.

On 4 July 2024, nearly 900 protesters and representatives of NFP, SOS Racism, and unions rallied at Horloge Square and subsequently took to the streets in Avignon (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to demonstrate. The event was part of a nationwide wave of demonstrations against far-right ideology and in support of an open society, and took place after the National Rally (RN) came first in the European elections in France and President Emmanuel Macron announced the dissolution of the National Assembly on 9 June 2024, prompting snap legislative elections and raising fears of a government led by the far-right party.

On 24 May 2022, overnight, health workers camped in front of the hospital of Morlaix at the call of the CFDT union. They denounced the lack of staff, which they claimed makes it impossible for them to take time off in the summer.

On 9 January 2021, a group of female activists affiliated with a regional women's rights association took part in a flash mob outside of a clinic in Macerata (Macerata, Marche) to protest against the regional government's declarations on the right to abortion and announced restraints on the administration of the abortion pill.
On 10 December 2022, residents of Plovdiv protested against plans to build a high-rise building along the river in the city, which would cut down on the green space in the area.

On 20 June 2020, about 700 people marched through Cobham village in Surrey for a Black Lives Matter protest, demonstrating against police brutality and systemic racism after the killing of an unarmed black man by a police officer in the United States.
On 24 April 2021, protesters organized by Djurfront demonstrated in Lund to oppose the use of animals for experiments at Lund University.

On 1 June 2024, at the call of PvdD, about 20 people protested in front of the Vion slaughterhouse in Tilburg (Noord-Brabant) against animal suffering. The protesters set up a cross to symbolize death in front of a tree nearby.

Around 1 December 2022 (as reported), an unknown number of activists of Last Renovation staged a protest in Boulogne-sur-Mer, blocking the Pont d'Issy bridge, presumably to demand more action against climate change. Eventually the police arrived and physically removed protesters from the road.

On 22 August 2022, environmental activists staged an action at a golf club in Saint-Germain-en-Laye. They condemned the use of water resources to maintain the golf pitch amid an unprecedented period of drought.

On 8 June 2020, at least 10 African and other foreign students organised by VOIS (Voices of International Students in Cyprus) rallied outside TRNC parliament in northern Nicosia to express their solidarity with the United States Black Lives Matter demonstrators and to protest against racist practices in Northern Cyprus. The students were also supported by representatives of LGBT groups.
On 20 December 2024, activists gathered for a rally in front of a local court in Inowroclaw, demanding proper investigation of a recent death of a young man, who lost his life in police custody.

On 9 June 2022, during an electoral rally for the administrative elections, residents demonstrated against the Puglia governor, denouncing the closure of an important hospital, in Terlizzi (Bari, Puglia).

On 18 October 2022, about 100 students gathered for a protest at blockage of Saint-Charles high school and Thiers high school in Marseille, against the Parcoursup secondary education allotment platform and the reform of the professional high schools, and in solidarity with Joliot Curie high school.

On 17 May 2023, as part of the national mobilization 'Without the house, without a future', university students affiliated with 'Uniattiva', 'Laboratorio Studentesco Autonomo', 'Vivere Ateneo', 'Onda Universitaria', 'Auletta99', 'UniXcento/Avanti', 'Nrg' and 'UniTrapani' pitched camping tents in delle Scienze boulevard in Palermo (Palermo, Sicilia) to protest against the current student housing crisis and the soaring cost of renting, and to demand urgent action by the government.

On 8 July 2022, 7 activists from Christian Climate Action, an affiliate of Extinction Rebellion, gathered for a protest, and disrupted the proceedings of the Church of England's General Synod, in York, against the church's alleged 55-million pound investment in fossil fuel companies.

On 11 July 2019, more than a thousand former workers of the 'Aluminij' company, mainly ethnic Croatians, and their supporters demonstrated in front of the Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) headquarters in Mostar, Bosnia and Herzegovina. Two people were arrested after an object was thrown at HDZ's president's car.

On 22 June 2024, people, including local elected officials and women, gathered in Hasparren (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to condemn gender-based violence after a woman was raped during the local fair the day prior.

On 19 March 2021, Fridays for Future activists staged a protest in Palma de Mallorca (Balearic Islands) to denounce the government's inaction on climate change and global warming. They said that the coronavirus pandemic is a symptom of a systemic crisis.

On 17 April 2021, a group of people wearing white protective suits and masks protested in Villeneuve-sur-Lot against coronavirus-related measures they perceived as infringements of freedom. They criticized the government's management of the health crisis and questioned official information and figures about the coronavirus health crisis.
On 16 March 2024, Fridays for Future members demonstrated in Sundsvall, Vasternorrland, to oppose aviation industry and calling on sustainable changes from the Scandinavian flag carrier.

On 15 September 2024, at the call of the 15 September Committee (Comitato 15 Settembre), around 300 people took to the streets of Trieste (Friuli-Venezia Giulia) to protest against wars and to call for the demilitarization of the area, and specifically the city's port. Local associations, including Together Free (Insieme liberi) and Sovereign and Popular Democracy (Democrazia sovrana e popolare), took part in the protest.
On 29 September 2022, several hundred people gathered for a protest in Tours, to demand better pay and against pension reform.

On 4 May 2024, health workers and administrative staff demonstrated outside the Hospital in Acireale (Sicilia) to demand the employees' parking area be expanded so as not to cause staff delays and poor services. Representatives of CGIL, CISL, and UIL were also present.

On 7 February 2022, around 600 people demonstrated in Potsdam against coronavirus-related measures including possible compulsory vaccination. People, including The Greens members, gathered at the call of SPD for a counter-demonstration and to call for solidarity and coronavirus vaccination.
On 11 September 2021, anti-vaxxer demonstrators protested in Dresden against coronavirus-related measures. A demonstrator insulted two journalists.

On 8 November 2021, around 100 persons blocked traffic in A-431 road in Almodovar del Rio (Cordoba, Andalucia), demanding better transport networks between Almodovar del Rio and Cordoba. The citizens' network platform #Nopasesdemi called the protest.

On 12 November 2024, students, at the nationwide call of SE, held a protest in Vitoria-Gasteiz (Pais Vasco) against the Valencian government, led by Carlos Mazon (PP), over its perceived negligence in handling recent floods that devastated parts of the region. Protesters argued that the government downplayed the severity of the disaster, causing a delayed response that left residents unprepared, resulting in loss of life and extensive property damage. They demanded Mazon's resignation as a consequence of the government's failure to protect the affected communities. The protest was followed by a strike.
On 10 July 2020, anti-government protesters rallied in Maribor, Slovenia. They protested against corruption, as well the government's response to the coronavirus.

On 14 February 2020, thousands of climate activists, including Greta Thunberg, gathered in Stockholm, demanding action on the climate emergency as part of a nationwide Friday For Future protest. The Socialist Justice party supported the event. Two convicted rap artists participated in the protest.

On 31 January 2023, Marconi high school students gathered in Giugliano in Campania (Napoli, Campania) to protest against the lack of an appropriate school venue after their school was declared unfit for use in May 2022. The students protested mainly because, since then, they had to attend afternoon classes and labs could not be accessible anymore.

On 28 March 2021, around 150 environmental activists protested in Montelimar to call on the government to implement concrete measures to tackle climate change. Protesters denounced that the climate and resilience bill was not stringent enough to meet the 2030 greenhouse gas emission reduction target. They also called for the 149 proposals from the Citizens Convention for Climate to be implemented. The event was part of a national day of protest called by Greenpeace, Friends of the Earth, International Movement ATD Fourth World, Attac, CARE, CCFD-Terre Solidaire (Catholic Committee against hunger and for development), XR, L214, FAGE, France Nature Environnement (French Nature Environment), Generations Futures (Future Generations), LDH, LPO - Ligue pour la protection des oiseaux (League for the Protection of Birds), Notre affaire a tous (Everyone's Business), OXFAM, SDN, EELV, Generation Ecologie (Ecology Generation), CFDT, and PS, before consideration by parliament of the government's climate and resilience bill, which they criticized.
On 27 February 2021, at least 75 Querdenken supporters protested in Heilbronn against the coronavirus protection measures.

On 20 March 2024, farmers with their vehicles blocked streets across the Bartoszyce district, protesting against what they see as a too low state support to the national agriculture and also criticizing ongoing imports of grains from Ukraine to the EU.

On 7 October 2021, representatives of local committees opposing coronavirus 'green pass' restrictions gathered outside the Madonna dei Sette Dolori Church in Pescara (Pescara, Abruzzo) to ask for the acknowledgment of their position from regional authorities.
On 30 April 2022, members of the yellow vests movement demonstrated in Paris. They called for social and fiscal justice.

On 10 September 2024, around 10 teachers demonstrated in Avignon (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur). The event was part of a nationwide strike movement called by SNUIPP-FSU, CGT-Educ'action, and SUD-Education to protest against the introduction of mandatory exams at primary schools, demand more state funding for public schools, and oppose the government's education reform, especially the introduction of level groups for students.

On 10 January 2022, in the evening, about 700 people, including Querdenken supporters and far-right activists, took to the streets, some taking part in 'walks' in Dortmund to protest against coronavirus-related measures. A counter-demonstration was organized, leading to verbal tension when both demonstration groups crossed ways. One person was identified by the police for failing to comply with COVID mask requirements.

On 6 May 2024, about 600 to 700 demonstrators, including students and university staff, demonstrated at the Roeterseiland campus of the University of Amsterdam (UvA) in Amsterdam (Noord-Holland) to show solidarity with the Palestinians and to call on the UvA and the Free University (VU) to stop economic and academic collaboration with Israel. The university called the police, who asked the demonstrators to leave. About 150 to 200 demonstrators did not leave, barricading themselves and blocking two bridges leading to the campus with construction fences. In the evening, about 10 counter-demonstrators clashed with the pro-Palestinian demonstrators, some of whom threw objects at the first group. Demonstrators also threw bricks and fireworks at the police, causing one police officer to suffer chronic hearing loss as a result. The police intervened and evacuated the demonstrators during the night and arrested 164 people. The event took place after similar actions were recorded on American campuses in previous days. The event was condemned by participants for disproportionate police violence at the time of reporting.

On 20 November 2024, people demonstrated outside the Parliament of Denmark in Copenhagen protesting the frequent removal of Greenlandic children from their families and their disproportionately high placement in Denmark compared to Greenland. The activists called on politicians to address the issue.
On 24 July 2021, hundreds of people protested against coronavirus related restrictions in Tampere.

On 11 December 2021, around 200 persons demonstrated in Montbeliard. They denounced coronavirus-related measures implemented by the government, including the obligation to wear masks, the approval of the vaccination for children under the age of 11 and changes in the bill on the obligation to provide the proof of the triple rather than the double vaccination to carry out professional and social activities.

On 10 January 2021, several hundred people staged a protest at the Westerpark in Amsterdam against fascism. The protest was organized following the assault on Capitol Hill by right-wing rioters in Washington DC, USA, earlier that week.

On 29 June 2020, citizens gathered in Sevilla to protest over the visit of the Kings of Spain in the South Polygon neighborhood. Protesters also complained over being one of the poorest neighborhoods in the country.
On 11 July 2023, Animal Save Movement activists demonstrated in Uppsala to oppose animal rights violations and to promote animal welfare.

On 12 June 2020, police officers gathered at the Palais place in Avignon and dropped their handcuffs on the floor. They protested against the declarations of the Minister of the Interior about implementing changes in the police arrest techniques that were made in response to a row of protests in the country against racism and police brutality.
On 1 February 2020, climate activists including a member of the youth wing of the Alternative party, staged a protest in Copenhagen to oppose operation of Shell company and use of fossil fuels.

On 4 March 2021, at night, around 50 persons, including independent professionals of the cultural sector occupied the Odeon theatre in Paris. They called denounced the impossibility to carry out their professional activity for a year, amid the coronavirus-restriction implemented by the government, called for financial assistance and demanded clear information on the conditions of reopening of cultural centers.

On 24 March 2025, a protest was organized in Tetovo demanding responsibility for the tragic accident that took place a couple of days earlier where 59 people were killed and 150 when a pyrotechnic device went off in a club and set it on fire. The event has shocked the Macedonian public and calls for widespread resignations have been demanded by protesters across the country.

On 20 May 2025, at the call of La Union local government (PP), around 200 residents of La Union protested outside the Ministry of Ecological Transition in Madrid - Centro (Madrid) to demand the regeneration of the Portman Bay, which was previously used as a mining wasteland, instead of sealing it off, citing environmental concerns. Protesters demanded compliance with the 2006 restoration agreement.

On 8 November 2019, parents led by the Parents United for Children Association held a protest in Sandanski against the new social services law, which they fear would enable social services to take their children away without their knowledge and consent.

On 1 September 2020, around 400 people protested in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg), in the city center, on the occasion of the 'Anti-War Day'. The protest was organized by Ver.di and attended by MLPD, FVC, and Environmental Union activists.
On 16 May 2018, dozens of members and supporterss of the Moldovan Liberal Party protested division of Moldova from Romania outside the Russian embassy in Chisinau.

On 21 October 2024, at the call of USS, several hundred Stahl employees as well as State Councilor and USS President Pierre-Yves Maillard (PS/SP) gathered on Federal Square in Bern (Bern) to protest against downsizing at the Gerlafingen factorry.

On 23 May 2022, about 125 people protested against coronavirus measures and the war in Ukraine in Wittenberg. Protesters denounced vaccination obligation which was recently declared lawful by the highest court.

On 11 January 2020, around 30 pro-independence campaigners from the Isle of Arran staged their own All Under One Banner march along the seafront around Brodick when ferries were cancelled and they were unable to reach the main event.
On 10 October 2021, around 250 cyclists protested in Luneburg at the call of BUND against the expansion of a highway (A39).

Around 12 October 2020 (as reported), North Wales Save Outdoor Education group held a banner protest at Beacon Climbing Centre in Caernarfon calling for the UK and Welsh Governments to allow overnight education trips for schools amid the coronavirus pandemic. The group also unfurled a banner at Dolbadarn Castle.
On 14 September 2022, people demonstrated in Tampere to oppose the possible construction of a highway passing through a recreational forest in the area.

On 7 January 2022, several far-right affiliates gathered in Acca Larentia street in Rome - Tuscolano (Roma, Lazio) to commemorate the victims of the 1978 Acca Larentia killings and denounce the role of the far left in the killings. Demonstrators performed the Fascist salute and several of them did not wear a mask in compliance with coronavirus restrictions. CasaPound took part in the demonstration.
On 29 January 2025, residents of Komiza gathered with pickets, declaring their solidarity with students and other protesters in Serbia.

On 28 March 2023, at 17:30, demonstrators took to the streets to protest in Ajaccio. The event was part of a tenth national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FIDL, FAGE, and MNL) to oppose the passing of a pension reform bill by means of Article 49.3 of the constitution by the government, and call for the withdrawal of the bill.

On 5 February 2025, people protested outside the US Consulate in Belfast - South (Northern Ireland) to denounce Donald Trump's actions during the early days of his second term as US president. The protesters criticized what they described as 'anti-democratic, draconian, and dangerous' measures, joining a broader wave of protests taking place across the US and internationally.

On 7 February 2023, around 3,500 employees of Deutsche Post protested at the call of Ver.di in Dortmund at the Friedensplatz (Nordrhein-Westfalen, Dortmund), to demand higher wages amid inflation. Thousands of employees in Nordrhein-Westfalen had gone on strike on that day.

On 21 December 2020, farmers drove dozens of vehicles across Santa Barbara and Tortosa (Tarragona), demanding urgent measures for their labor sector. They demanded to allocate the financial aid from the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) of the European Union to the most affected labor sectors due to the coronavirus pandemic.

Around 22 November 2020 (as reported), seasonal workers gathered outside the Federturismo offices in Rimini to protest against the working conditions of people employed in the tourism industry. The demonstration was supported by the USB labor union.

On 31 January 2025, more than 50 people gathered in Latronquiere (Occitanie) to protest against the installation of windmills on the Haut-Segala plateau. They complained that the installation was located 1000m from dwellings.
On 6 June 2021, local residents gathered in Sodermalm district of Stockholm to demonstrate for preservation of Liljeholmsbadet floating swimming pool that is planned to be closed.
On 25 October 2020, activists, mostly women, gathered for a rally in Zory protesting against restrictions of abortions in Poland. The event was coordinated by the Women's Strike.

On 11 December 2024, more than 100 public employees, called by CCOO, UGT, ANPE, USO, the Federation of Associations of Education Inspectors and Inspecting Officers (Federacion de Asociaciones de Inspectores e Inspectoras de Educacion - ADIDE), the Union of Education Inspectors (Union Sindical de Inspectores de Educacion - USIE), the Federal Police Union (Union Federal de Policia - UFP), ACAIP, and the Independent Union of the Tax Agency (Sindicato Independiente de la Agencia Tributaria - SIAT), protested outside Muface's headquarters in Barcelona - L'Eixample (Cataluna) to defend Muface, a mutual healthcare system, against potential integration into the public health system.
On 11 February 2021, HB activists held a protest in Valle de Trapaga-Trapagaran (Pais Vasco) to demand the independence of the Basque country and the amnesty of all convicted ETA armed group members.

On 19 May 2025, 100-150 Turkish Cypriots and children of mixed marriages between a Turkish Cypriot and a Turkish parent, marched from the buffer zone to the Nicosia District Office as the 'Association of the Uncredentialled' or 'Association of the Unidentified', demanding they be given citizenship of the Republic of Cyprus and they attempted a mass application. The protesters were holding placards and shouting slogans in Turkish. There was police presence, but there was no need for intervention. Since 2007 the Republic of Cyprus would deny citizenship to the children of mixed marriages, if one of their parents were Turkish nationals who entered and resided in the north after 1974 (the year of the Turkish invasion).
On 29 June 2022, at the call of the RESF, around 30 persons including the deputy mayor and teachers demonstrated in Nanterre to denounce the expulsion from French territory of a Romanian family.
On 6 September 2020, local residents protested in Kraljske Bare, Montenegro, against construction of a mini hydro power plant, citing environmental concerns.
On 1 October 2020, over 50 workers of Alu Iberica (former Alcoa) protested in A Coruna to demand the government to intervene to save the job positions that are at risk in the plant.

On 24 April 2021, people protested in Plevenon against the failure to carry out votes during the municipal councils due to the resignation of the municipal councilors. They called for the budget to be voted.

On 3 November 2023, at the call of German Peace Society-United War Opponents (DFG-VK) Baden-Wurttemberg, the Tubingen Society for Culture of Peace and Pax Christi Rottenburg-Stuttgart, about 100 people, including left-wing affiliates and Christians, gathered for a pro-Palestinian rally in Stuttgart (Baden-Wurttemberg), expressing solidarity with the Palestinian population and condemning the Israeli military campaign in the Gaza Strip.
On 12 August 2021, protesters gathered in Viljandi to oppose plans to cut approximately 50 trees to build a sidewalk and bicycle path along a street in the city center.

On 17 September 2020, around 50 persons gathered in Flers, at the call of the CGT union. They demonstrated for the 'rights of workers' following the coronavirus pandemic, as part of a national day of protests. They demanded a ban on staff cuts, more resources for public services and better working conditions.

On 27 October 2021, in the morning, between 100 and 200 Genovesi high school students gathered outside San Giacomo palace in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to call for the reopening of their school's city center branch. The deputy mayor for education reportedly took part in the protest, supporting the students' action but also urging them to go back to classrooms to make up for the lost time due to coronavirus.

On 1 May 2023, members of the Irish Communities Together group gathered outside Taoiseach (Prime Minster) Leo Varadkar's home in Dublin. Some group members held several slogans, including 'concerned communities families and parents'. The protest was organized amid calls for legislation to stop protests outside public representatives' homes.
On 16 August 2021, residents of Szczecin gathered for a rally, protesting against reduction of green places in the city.

On 25 November 2021, during the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, around 200 citizens gathered in Almeria (Andalucia) to protest against gender-based violence. The Feminist Action Platform was involved in the protest.

On 28 June 2023, lawyers gathered in A Coruna (Galicia) as part of their ongoing protest to demand a salary increase, that maternity and paternity leave be respected, and better working conditions, among other claims.

On 11 March 2023, around 500 people staged a protest in Saint-Marcelin. The event was part of a seventh national and cross-sector day of strike and protest called by CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform.

On 9 July 2022, 7 XR activists occupied an ING bank office in Den Bosch (Noord-Brabant) to denounce the bank's investments in fossil fuels. Five activists who stayed after the bank's closing time were arrested by the police.
On 10 January 2022, people took to the streets, gathering in two locations, in Eberswalde to protest against coronavirus-related measures. A counter-protest was organized.

On 7 April 2021, market vendors from across the Cosenza province gathered, at the call of the ANA and UGL trade unions, outside the Stefano Rizzo stadium in Rossano (Cosenza, Calabria) to protest against continued coronavirus restrictions to their activities and demand a clear roadmap for the reopening of their businesses from public authorities.
On 15 May 2021, around 1000 pro-Palestine protesters, including several activists (Generation.s, LFI, PCF), demonstrated in Nantes to call for an immediate end to the Israeli bombing in Palestine.

On 25 January 2025, CNRS (National Centre for Scientific Research) researchers gathered in Toulouse (Occitanie) to demonstrate against a proposed 'Key Labs' reform of research funding aimed at concentrating funding on 25% of research units designated as 'Key Labs' for a five-year period, prioritizing those considered to be of 'world-class' standing, which would result in reduced funding for the remaining 75% of laboratories.
On 8 March 2025, 1,300 people protested in Jaen (Andalucia) to demand gender equality on the occasion of International Women's Day.

On 7 February 2025, striking Lidl workers gathered in Rousset (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to demonstrate. The event was part of a national day of strike and demonstration called by CGT, CFDT, FO, CFE-CGC, and CFTC to denounce poor working conditions, low staffing levels, and management's plan to open all stores every Sunday starting from 1 June 2025.

On 20 October 2020, primary care physicians (general practitioners) called by the Malaga Medical Union gathered in Malaga to protest about excessive work overload during the coronavirus pandemic. Protesters demanded more human and material resources be allocated to the public health services.
On 15 June 2022, employees of OASTH, the Organisation of Urban Transportation in Thessaloniki, participated in a strike-protest for the renewal of their collective labor agreement and other issues.

On 30 May 2021, residents and members of Living Rent gathered in Edinburgh to protest the planned conversion of the old Tynecastle School into purpose-built student accommodation. They called for more social housing and affordable properties to meet local needs instead. Members of the National Union of Students, University and College Union and local councilors joined the protest.
On 30 July 2019, several people protested outside the Supreme Council of Magistrature, demanding the cleaning of the judicial system.

On 26 March 2025, in the morning, at the call of parents' groups and local elected officials, around 40 people, including parents of pupils and municipal representatives, blocked access to the school in Saint-Genard (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to protest the planned closure of the site's only class at the start of the 2025 school year.

On 14 May 2021, pro-Israeli and pro-Palestine activists gathered near the embassy of Israel in Prague, supporting their respective sides in the ongoing conflict. No violent interactions were reported.

On 4 February 2021, around 500 persons demonstrated in Caen at the call of the CGT, SUD, FSU, UNEF, UNL, MNL and FIDL unions. They denounced precariousness and called for the development of public services, more rights and better working conditions for workers and social justice.
On 8 March 2024, on the occasion of International Women's Day, around 200 people gathered in Gotha (Thuringen) to protest against patriarchal structures.

On 10 October 2024, lawyers gathered outside the Court of Justice in Agen (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to express solidarity with all persecuted lawyers worldwide, notably imprisoned Tunisian Lawyer Sonia Dahmani.

On 15 September 2022, students held a protest at the Faculty of Law of the University of Granada in Granada (Andalucia) against the presence of former deputy of Vox Macarena Olona who starred in an act in the Auditorium organized by the Forum of Concord.
On 6 March 2022, around 4,000 people, including elected officials, demonstrated in Bremen at the call of several organizations (DGB, The Greens) against the war in Ukraine and the Russian government.

On 5 January 2024, parents of children with disabilities protested in front of the city council in Banja Luka, demanding urgent payment of social contributions. The protesters voiced that they were left for five months without any financial support.
On 4 November 2023, around 200 citizens, including Palestinians, marched for Palestine in Groningen (Groningen), expressing solidarity with the Palestinian population.

On 20 March 2025, around half a dozen people gathered in the public gallery of the House of Lords in London - Westminster (England) to demand the abolition of the unelected chamber. The protesters disrupted the session by throwing leaflets, shouting, and singing before being escorted out by security. The action caused a brief adjournment of the House.
On 7 February 2024, around 150 AUR members and supporters protested in Targu Mures, condemning the intention to set the same date for European elections and local elections.

On 7 October 2020, farmers affiliated to AgroUnia blocked many roads across Poland, including in Janowiec Wielkopolski. They were protesting about newly proposed laws on agriculture and protection of animals.

On 21 August 2021, around 1,700 persons demonstrated in Quimper. They called for the withdrawal of a coronavirus-related bill on the obligation to provide the proof of the double vaccination to resume their professional and social activities.
On 8 December 2023, around 100 court clerks protested outside the Appeal Court in Constanta, demanding wage increases and the payment of wage arrears.
On 26 September 2022, people protested in Pasewalk to demand an energy cap amid rising prices and current energy policies.
On 8 March 2020, Augusta Prison inmates shouted and hit the cells' bars to demonstrate against the measures imposed to contain the spread of coronavirus, including restrictions on family visits.
On 1 July 2020, Belarusians protested in Nice. They protested for the release of political prisoners.

On 12 December 2024, at the call of SNEP-FSU, around 30 striking teachers gathered for a picket line outside the Jouffroy d'Abbans school in Sochaux (Bourgogne-Franche-Comte) to protest against the arrest of one of their colleagues for allegedly slapping a student in the face.

On 31 October 2022, farmers in 20 tractors, associated with federation of farmers' unions (FDSEA) and the Young Farmers of Tarn-et-Garonne, gathered for a protest and blocked a bridge in Cordes-Tolosannes, against the increase in charges for the bridge and the discrepancy between increasing fuel prices and their salaries. The protesters dumped manure and tires on the bridge to block the passage.

On 10 June 2023, at the call of the alliance 'Ingolstadt is colorful', numerous people, including members of FFF, Antifa, elected officials (The Greens, The Left), a protestant pastor, and the mayor (SPD), demonstrated on Carraraplatz in Ingolstadt against historical revisionism, fascism, far-right extremism, and an event of the revisionist association ZFI - Ingolstadt Research Institute for Contemporary Historical Research.

On 3 June 2024, at the call of several farmers' organizations (Ataca, the Aega association, GPC, Bagea, Sepricas, Magin, Semilla y Belarra, the 6F Platform, Aguidiru, the Association of Free Farmers and Ranchers, Aliv, Decaleon, Sepriman and Agrygal, Adecgu, Adeccu, and the French Independent Movement), farmers with tractors participated in a motorcade, driving at a slow pace through Astigarraga (Pais Vasco), to demonstrate. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement against the ratification of the EU's free-trade agreements until partner third countries comply with the EU's agricultural standards, and in favor of fair production prices for Spanish farmers, relief measures to offset the consequences of droughts and of the import of agricultural products from Ukraine, as well as better working and social conditions in their sector.

On 23 April 2021, about 10 activists affiliated with the movement Extinction Rebellion gathered for a rally in Krakow, declaring support to their fellow activists detained at a local police station and demanding their immediate release.

On 19 October 2020, around 400 persons, including teachers, the mayor, representatives of the LDH and of the Catholic and Muslim religion gathered in front of the city hall in Abbeville. They observed a minute of silence as part of a national tribute to a teacher, deadly attacked days before. They also demonstrated for freedom of speech.

On 1 October 2024, around 300 people demonstrated in Belfort (Bourgogne-Franche-Comte). The event was part of a nationwide strike and demonstration day called by CGT, SUD, and FSU to demand better public service, protest against state budget cuts, and defend workers' rights. The protesters also criticized what they saw as an undemocratic rightward shift in the government, arguing that President Emmanuel Macron ignored the strong performance of the left in the legislative elections by appointing Michel Barnier (LR) as Prime Minister.
