On 7 December 2023, at the call of CGIL and UIL, around 70 people and workers demonstrated in Ravenna (Emilia-Romagna) against the decision of the Austria-based multinational Mayr-Melnhof to close the Farmografica production plant in Cervia, where 92 people are employed. Mayor of Cervia Massimo Medri (Civic List) and mayor of Ravenna Michele De Pascale (PD) were present.

On 24 January 2025, workers of Inditex, called by CCOO, held a protest outside the Massimo Dutti shop in Ciudad Real (Castilla-La Mancha) against its closure, arguing it would result in the layoff of 13 employees or their relocation to other Inditex stores, primarily in Madrid, without compensation for relocation costs. The protesters criticized Inditex's strategy of focusing on larger stores in major cities while shutting down smaller outlets in smaller cities, highlighting the impact on long-serving employees.

On 22 September 2020, tens of thousands of people, including members of Democratic Bulgaria, demonstrated in Sofia demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Borisov and chief prosecutor Geshev over alleged corruption and links to mafia. Several clashes with the police broke out after the demonstrators tried to go through the police cordon. The demonstrators threw glass bottles, two firework bombs, eggs and cobble stone at the law enforcers. Three police officers were injured, several people were arrested.

On 24 September 2022, over 300 motorcyclists, coordinated by the International Union for the Defense of Motorcyclists (IMU), demonstrated in Bilbao (Bizkaia, Pais Vasco) to demand more security and mobility measures.
On 19 February 2021, miners protested outside the coal mine in Vulcan, demanding the payment of the delayed salaries and the clarification of the situation around the Hunedoara Energetic Complex.

On 11 July 2022, a group of farmers staged a protest action in Barneveld, blocking the road with tractors while hanging up reversed Dutch flags throughout the town to denounce the new Dutch nitrogen regulations.
On 6 June 2022, people demonstrated in Leverkusen against plans to cut down 300 trees for flood protection.

On 24 August 2023, around 100 workers and trade union activists staged a union blockade of a construction site in Frederiksberg, Hovedstaden, demanding the subcontractor to act in accordance with the collective bargaining agreement.

On 8 October 2020, an unknown number of people staged a protest on Het Plein in Den Haag against the coronavirus protection laws of the Dutch government and its impact on individual freedom. Police forces intervened after some protesters refused to go home, resulting in 82 arrests.
On 22 May 2021, pro-Palestinian protesters driving around 30 cars staged a 'go-slow' protest in Stoke-on-Trent in opposition to the perceived persecution of Palestinians by the Israeli state.
On 6 November 2020, activists, mostly women, gathered for a rally in Strzelce, protesting against restrictions of abortions in Poland. The event was coordinated by the Women's Strike.

On 7 February 2020, at least 100 people, most of them school students and accompanying teachers, took part in a flash mob in Marino to protest against bullying and cyberbullying. The protest was organised as part of the 'Day against bullying and cyberbullying'.

On 16 June 2020, Stram Kurs held an anti-Islamic demonstration in Korsor. Over 100 police officers were present to protect the party's leader. On the same day, the leader announced he would reduce the number of demonstrations as he will no longer be protected by security personnel.

On 18 June 2024, an unknown number of XR activists protested in front of the offices of the AIG and Marsh insurance companies in Brussels - Ixelles (Brussels) to denounce their funding of the EACOP crude oil pipeline project that threatens wildlife habitats in Africa.
On 19 June 2021, an unknown number of people staged a protest in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles against the imminent establishment of a tram connection between Brussels center and Neder-Over-Heembeek.

On 9 March 2020, a collective of teachers and parents demonstrated in Saint-Raphael against the threat of expulsion hanging over a Kosovar family. They also asked the prefecture to re-examine their case and to suspend the expulsion procedure. The Kosovar family was also present at the demonstration.

On 4 September 2023, at the call of 'Osservatorio Paola Labriola' and the non-profit organization 'La Giraffa', dozens of people staged a picket in front of the former mental health center in the Liberta neighborhood of Bari (Puglia, Bari) to commemorate psychiatrist Paola Labriola, killed on 4 September 2013 by a patient. Demonstrators also demand the reopening of the mental health center. Municipal Councilor Paola Romano (PD) and vice president of the Bari Medical Association Franco Lavalle were present.
On 15 September 2022, farmers gathered for a protest ride around Hradec Kralove, demanding higher support for the Czech agriculture.

On 20 January 2024, at the call of RESCOP, thousands of people protested in Vitoria-Gasteiz (Pais Vasco) in solidarity with the Palestinian people and against Israeli violence amid the ongoing war in the Gaza Strip.

On 1 December 2022, around 350 general practitioners staged a protest in front of the Part-Dieu train station in Lyon to demand higher remuneration and better wage benefits. The protest was an initiative of the Medecins pour Demain movement and took place in the context of a general strike of liberal general practitioners and biomedical laboratories throughout the country on 1 and 2 December 2022.

On 15 September 2022, at the call of FISASCAT CISL, around 30 RAI Torino logistics employees gathered in front of the RAI headquarters in Via Verdi in Torino (Torino, Piemonte) to demand the payment of the last five salaries, which they claimed they still had not received.

On 21 June 2023, parents of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) held a protest in London (England) against the nationwide SEND reforms. The event was part of a national day of action.
On 3 May 2024, people, called by Neighbors' Association Nuevo Ventanielles (Asociacion Vecinal Nuevo Ventanielles) held a protest in Oviedo (Asturias) to demand an increase of medical personnel.

On 6 June 2020, nearly 200 people, including BLM activists, demonstrated in Basel to denounce systemic racism, police brutality, and lack of justice in Switzerland and the rest of the world. They also paid tribute to a African-American man killed by the police in Minneapolis on 25 May 2020.
On 11 February 2022, Identitarian Movement gathered in front of Aalborg Theatre to oppose the ongoing performance that they believe puts their movement in a negative light.

On 23 October 2021, activists gathered for a rally in Michalowo, demanding higher solidarity with refugees stranded at the Polish-Belarusian border. Women, in particular, were protesting against not helping other women and children.
On 8 October 2020, members of Oxford Friends of the Earth rallied in Botley calling for urgent action to cut the 'unacceptable' levels of pollution across Oxfordshire.

On 5 May 2022, members of disabled and special needs community in Bydgoszcz protested in solidarity with fellow special needs communities in Ukraine. They claim the needs of their community often get overlooked, and they can imagine how much worse it has gotten since the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine.

On 15 March 2022, around 500,000 people marched from Budapest - II (Budapest) as part of the Peace March, led by Fidesz MPs and the COF-COKA coalition, against the war in Ukraine, without condemning the Russian aggression, and condemning the leftist opposition's statements and electoral program, as well as the European Union for violating the sovereignty of Hungary. Croatian Hungarians, as well as the UGL labour union from Italy, and other Hungarian trade unions, joined the rally.
Around 21 November 2023, (as reported) people demonstrated in Vadso, Troms og Finnmark, to show support and solidarity with the people of Palestine amid the ongoing Israeli offensive in Gaza.

On 13 September 2023, refugees and asylum seekers held at the port of Lampedusa (Sicilia, Agrigento) demanded to be allowed to leave, some of them trying to break through the police cordon and exiting the port's restricted area. Police responded by charging the rioters and managed to restore order.
On 7 February 2020, activists of UZUS protested in front of the National Assembly in Belgrade, Serbia, against reality TV programs.
On 28 January 2021, high school students protested outside of the Ministry of Education in Skopje-Centar, demanding changes to the state graduation exam.
On 26 October 2022, students demonstrated in Volda (More og Romsdal County) to oppose the government's proposal to introduce tuition fees to international students.

On 30 May 2023, around 20 civil servants of the administration of justice held a protest in Zamora (Castilla y Leon) as part of their ongoing protest to demand a dignified work, a salary raise, and against the Organic Law of Organizational Efficiency (LOEO). The protest was summoned by STAJ, CSIF, UGT, and CCOO.
On 31 May 2022, civil servants protested in front of the parliament building in Sarajevo, demanding an appropriate collective agreement and improved salaries.

On 25 July 2024, about 25 activists, including deputies for the Confederation, gathered in Warsaw near the parliament building, protesting against the recently concluded security treaty between Poland and Ukraine.

On 25 November 2024, on the occasion of the International Day against Violence against Women, at the call of representatives from various organizations, including AI and the Soroptimist Club, and under the motto 'No to Violence Against Women', people gathered in Passau (Bayern) to raise awareness about toxic relationships and gender-based violence, with a focus on prevention and support for victims. The event featured orange displays to symbolize a future free from violence against women.

On 6 June 2023, in the morning, people took to the streets of Cosne-Cours-sur-Loire to demonstrate. The event was part of a 14th national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FAGE, FIDL, and MNL) to call for the withdrawal of the government's pension reform and better wealth distribution.
On 11 March 2021, health workers protested in Colmar because they are not entitled to a monthly salary increase that hospital health workers have been granted by the Segur agreements.

On 11 July 2020, over two hundred people gathered in Reggio Calabria (Reggio di Calabria, Calabria) under the banner 'Let's Remain Free' to protest against a draft law against homotransphobia. Protesters claimed that such a law would affect their freedom of expression, education, religion, social and political aggregation.

On 29 May 2021, around 500 British armed forces veterans and their supporters gathered in Brecon to demonstrate in support of former soldiers who are facing trials for the murder of civilians in Northern Ireland during The Troubles. This event was organized by Justice for Northern Ireland Veterans.

On 13 December 2023, at the call of CGT, CNT, FSU, the French Lawyers' Union (SAF), and SUD, around 50 people gathered on Strasbourg Street in Nantes (Pays de la Loire) to protest against demonstrations of far-right groups paying tribute to Thomas, a 16-year-old youth who was stabbed and consequently died after a brawl in Crepol on 18 November 2023, claiming he was killed because he was white.

On 9 January 2024, farmers driving almost 30 tractors staged a protest in Emden (Niedersachsen) by blocking the entrance to the Volkswagen Factory; the police intervened to disperse the gathering. The event was part of a nationwide demonstration movement called by farmers to denounce the government's plan to cut agricultural sector subsidies.

On 21 August 2023, pensioners gathered in Tetovo to demand a linear or equal increase of pensions, claiming that inflation and the high cost of living eat away at their budget. Protests were organized in several Macedonian cities and towns.

On 21 February 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of the initiative 'Action Youth' (Aktion Jugend), around 300 people, including Mayor Dirk Oetzel (SPD) and Federal Parliament Member Awet Tesfaiesus (The Greens), gathered in Hessisch Lichtenau (Hessen) to protest in defense of democracy and against hate and violence. The event was part of a nationwide protest movement focused on defending democracy ahead of the 2025 federal elections.

On 30 October 2020, people waving placards protested outside a Aldridge-Brownhills MP's constituency office in Aldridge as a protest over the Conservative Party MP's vote not to extend free school meals for pupils during holidays in England until Easter 2021.

On 29 May 2024, citizens gathered in Dugo Selo, demanding that the local authorities improve the streets' signalization and overall infrastructure contributing to citizens' safety. The protest is triggered by the tragic event in which a truck ran over a young girl.

On 29 July 2022, road construction workers gathered in Blagoevgrad to protests the delays in payment they have been facing for months, as the issue of road construction contracts being politicized sparks a three-day series of protests nationwide. Three-day protests have been organized nationwide and the protesters have announced a wider blockade of the road system in the upcoming months.

On 7 September 2024, at the call of Poitiers Palestine, 150 people demonstrated from the town hall to the prefecture in Poitiers (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) in solidarity with Gaza, Palestinians, and their children. They denounced an Israeli army killing a civilian population and defined the country's actions as an '11-month genocide'.
On 11 September 2022, UP members staged a demonstration in Catania (Catania, Sicilia) to ask for the introduction of a minimum wage of 10 euros per hour.

On 18 February 2023, at the call of Alliance for Peace (Bundnis fur Frieden) which includes BPD, Reich Citizens, Freedom Parade, Radio Dawn (Radio Morgenrote), and Fumigation for Mother Earth (Rauchern fur Mutter Erde), people demonstrated at Alexanderplatz in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) for a far-right protest under the motto 'Peace now'. Grannies Against the Right gathered for a counter-demonstration.

On 26 July 2023, representatives of KTAMS, KAMU-SEN and KAMU-IS, rallied outside the courthouse in Northern Nicosia and made statements, during a 1-hour strike, to protest over legal problems, understaffing and the lack of building infrastructure.

On 25 December 2020, about 100 residents of Aspropyrgos - mainly youths - hurled rocks and flares at MAT riot police in NATO Avenue. They were likely demonstrating against the extension of a hard lockdown in Aspropyrgos and Eleusis due to their heavy coronavirus epidemiological burden.

On 14 April 2024, under the motto 'Solidarity with Daniela', up to 25 people staged a protest in front of the women's prison in Vechta (Niedersachsen) in solidarity with the imprisoned ex-RAF activist Daniela Klette.

On 28 November 2024, students and academics from UHasselt in Hasselt (Vlaanderen) and other Belgian universities staged a national walkout a day before the International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People. They protested against human rights violations in Palestine and demanded that Belgian universities end collaborations with Israeli institutions. The protesters also called for an academic boycott, Israel's exclusion from Horizon Europe, and a military embargo on Israel.
On 15 November 2021, Seb Moulinex workers gathered in Mayenne to demand better salaries and recognition of their work.

On 5 August 2021, several hundred farmers affiliated with AgroUnia blocked by their machines a highway near Piotrkow Trybunalski. They were criticizing allegedly harmful and negligent national policy on agriculture and demanding higher support.
On 7 November 2022, people gathered in Naunhof to call for peace, freedom and sovereignty. They criticized the government's energy policies and coronavirus-related measures.
On 17 May 2023, about 130 young people protested in Kruibeke, to demand 'space to be young', party venues in the town, and tolerance towards young people.

On 6 October 2023, about 30 people staged a protest in front of the municipal police headquarters in Venezia (Venezia, Veneto) to protest against the decision to charge a gondolier of contempt of a public official for failing to provide his identification when he staged a protest against water traffic on board of his gondola prior to the historical regatta. 'Gruppo 25 aprile' and 'Tutta la citta insieme' representatives, including a municipal councilor, took part in the demonstration.
On 22 May 2024, at the call of CGT, striking Gepor employees blocked access to the port in Illange (Grand Est) to protest against the sale of their company and demand safe jobs.

On 13 May 2021, potato farmers from the Famagusta district handed out sacks of potatoes and carnations to oncoming cars at the Xylofagou exit of the Larnaca-Famagusta highway to raise awareness about difficulties in selling their produce as exports have stopped due to businesses being shuttered because of the coronavirus pandemic and other problems such as low rainfall. The protesters requested financial support by the government.

On 1 December 2023, unionized truck drivers for the 25th day blocked with their vehicles the border crossing point with Ukraine in Hrebenne. They were condemning allegedly unfair conditions for Ukrainian transport and trade companies and demanded stronger state oversight.
On 20 June 2020, around 80 people protested in Munchen against the real estate company Dawonia and for affordable rent.

On 17 May 2023, farmers protested and blocked the roads with tractors in Sombor, voicing their dissatisfaction with the failed agreement with the government regarding their demands to increase the subsidies and determine the minimum purchase price of milk.
On 7 May 2024, health workers demonstrated outside the Finnish Parliament in Helsinki to oppose planned cuts to the healthcare sector.

On 1 February 2025, around 500 people, including members of unspecified unions, political groups, and student organizations, demonstrated near the Palais des Congres in Montelimar (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to protest a rally held by Jordan Bardella, leader of the far-right Rassemblement National (RN). Protesters condemned the party's far-right ideology, anti-immigration stance, and racism.

On 8 October 2022, members of the Revolt of Empty Spain (La Revuelta de la Espana Vaciada) platform held a protest in Burgos (Burgos, Castilla y Leon) to ask the Government to create a new statute for the sector that would defend their labor rights and improve the management of forest fires, as well as their prevention.
Around 19 November 2021 (as reported), at the call of the CP, farmers gathered in front of a supermarket in Millau, to denounce the measures adopted by the government against the bird flue.
On 4 December 2021, around 90 people protested in Oschatz against coronavirus-related measures.
On 29 January 2022, around 150 people protested in Ibiza (Balearic Islands) against the coronavirus passport certificate.

On 12 March 2025, students of the Higher School of Electrical Engineering and Computing Vocational Studies gathered in Vojvode Stepe Street in Belgrade - Vozdovac to observe 15 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign. The aim was to honor the victims and emphasize their demands for the accountability for the loss of 15 lives following the collapse of a concrete canopy at the Novi Sad railway station.

On 9 May 2020, citizens protested from their balconies in Mali Zvornik, Serbia, against the government. The protest was initiated by Don't Let Belgrade D(r)own, in response to what they say is a 'dictatorship, laid bare by the COVID-19'.

On 10 July 2021, dozens of ACORN Union members and supporters gathered in Cambridge to take part in a protest swim in the River Cam against local landowners including Cambridge University implementing measures to discourage local residents from swimming in the River Cam and the land around it, as well as the Police, Crime Sentencing and Courts Bill which activists say will restrict the public's right to roam and disproportionately affect Traveler and Romani communities.

On 18 October 2020, nearly 500 persons, including teachers, gathered in Perigueux. They denounced terrorism and fundamentalism after the deadly attack against a teacher days before, and demonstrated for freedom of speech.

On 31 January 2025, health workers gathered in front of the Betanija Maternity Hospital in Novi Sad to observe 15 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign, to honor the victims who lost their lives following the collapse of a concrete canopy at the Novi Sad train station and demand accountability for their deaths.
On 14 February 2020, a Fridays For Future climate strike gathered in Salo, demanding climate action. No students seemed to be in attendance.
On 30 January 2020, farmers protested in Kassel against the tightening of the Fertilizing Ordinance and the agrarian investment plan in form of multi-billion-dollar aid.
On 15 August 2022, around 70 people demonstrated in Grossenhain against coronavirus-related measures as they gathered for a 'Monday Walk' - name given to such demonstration.

On 9 February 2022, sports association representatives gathered in Spinea (Venezia, Veneto) to protest against their temporary transfer to less well-equipped facilities following the closure of the Mantegna gym complex until video cameras and an entry card system are installed due to recent acts of vandalism.

On 20 January 2020, a dozen of lawyers and around fifty CGT activists protested in front of the AstraZeneca pharmaceutical factory in Dunkerque, that the French President was visiting. Police officers intervened and two lawyers were arrested.

On 29 June 2020, around twenty Monteco waste collectors gathered outside Lecce Prefecture to protest against the non-compliance with the national collective agreement. The demonstration was organised by the Italian Labour Unions FIADEL and CISL.
On 22 November 2021, hairdressers protested in Valencia (Valencian community), calling on the government to reduce the VAT rate (from 21% to 10%) applied to their labour sector.

On 25 November 2020, nearly 2,000 persons gathered in Nantes at the call of feminist organizations. They denounced sexist and sexual violence against women. The police intervened and used tear gas on protesters. They also made one arrest.

On 10 February 2022, in the morning, families of children attending local schools and school lunch service workers gathered outside the town hall of Carovigno (Brindisi, Puglia) to protest against the suspension of school lunch services.

On 5 October 2024, around 350 people gathered in Nantes (Pays de la Loire) to express solidarity with Palestinians and call for an immediate halt to Israeli military operations in Gaza and Lebanon and economic sanctions against Israel.

On 4 March 2023, tens of members of KNE, school and university students and members of Labour associations, rallied and marched in Thessaloniki carrying placards and banners over the Tempe rail disaster, the worst in Greece's history, and the longstanding deficiencies of Greece's railways, demanding justice and a full inquiry.

On 6 June 2023, between 540 (according to police) and 3,000 (unions) people took to the streets of Beauvais (Hauts-de-France) to demonstrate. The event was part of a 14th national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FAGE, FIDL, and MNL) to call for the withdrawal of the government's pension reform and better wealth distribution.

On 17 January 2022, up to 600 people, including far-right activists, took to the streets for an unregistered 'walk' in Magdeburg to denounce coronavirus-related measures. Pepper spray was used and one male demonstrator threw a bottle at police officers. About 350 people simultaneously gathered at the Old Market under the slogan 'Solidarity through the pandemic' to demonstrate in favor of compliance with coronavirus-related measures.

On 19 May 2021, demonstrators, including Socialist People's Party and Red-Green Alliance members, gathered in Gladsaxe to oppose the repatriation of Syrian refugees as certain parts of Syria are now considered safe by the Danish government. The demonstration was a part of the nationwide protest action held in more than 23 cities across the country.

On 24 February 2024, around 200 people, mostly members of Betyarsereg and MHM MPs, protested in Sopron, condemning the recently discovered pedophile pardoning, but also against migration and against the building of battery plants.

Around 3 October 2020, over a dozen citizens gathered in Irun (Pais Vasco) to express support to a former member of 'Basque homeland and freedom' (ETA) held in prison who started a hunger strike. Protesters also claimed for the independence of the Basque Country.

On 10 January 2025, about 2500 Slovak activists gathered for a rally in Presov, protesting against violations of democratic principles in the country. In particular they criticized the PM's recent unscheduled visit to Russia and asserted their support for Ukraine.

On 24 December 2023, around 130 people gathered before the PSOE headquarters in Madrid - Moncloa-Aravaca (Madrid) as part of an ongoing protest against the deal that Spain's PSOE Prime Minister, Pedro Sanchez, sealed with JuntsXCat and ERC, which also includes an amnesty pact.

On 17 June 2020, around 1500 people staged a protest at Haarlemmerhout in Haarlem against racism and police violence in the context of worldwide Black Lives Matter protests. Kick Out Zwarte Piet took part in the protest.
On 16 January 2021, several hundred people demonstrated in Carcassonne. They called for the removal of the 'comprehensive security' bill.
On 5 April 2024, Women's Strike movement activists demonstrated in Skovde, Vastra Gotaland, in support of women's rights and to oppose violence against women.

On 13 November 2020, climate activists blocked the Laxenburger Street near the A23 highway in Vienna - Favoriten and protested with the motto 'Forest instead of asphalt' against the construction of the A49 motorway in Germany and the subsequent clearing of the Danninger Forest.
On 13 September 2021, nurses gathered in front of Herlev Hospital in Herlev to demand an increase in wages for healthcare workers and to show dissatisfaction with the outcome of the nurses' strike.

On 1 April 2024, republican dissident groups held a march in Derry - Cityside (Northern Ireland) to mark the anniversary of the Easter Rising. The event was organized by the Derry 1916 Commemoration Committee. At the end of the parade, a number of young people with masks covering their faces threw petrol bombs at PSNI cars and journalists. There was no report of injuries.
On 12 September 2022, 80-100 people, mostly students and teachers, protested outside the Deak Ferenc school in Szeged in support of the teachers' strike for better wages and more teaching staff.

On 19 November 2022, between 30 and 40 Yellow Vests gathered in Soissons, on the occasion of the fourth year of the movement, to demand higher wages amid inflation and talk about politics, inflation and the cost of living.

On 12 June 2023, several Revival party members and supporters protested in support of better relations with Russia in front of the Russian embassy in Chisinau - Buiucani. A group of counter-protesters condemned Russia's terrorist acts in Ukraine.

On 2 March 2024, as part of an ongoing picket, farmers demonstrated in Foggia (Puglia) with their tractors. The event was part of a national farmers' demonstration movement against the government's plan to cut agricultural sector subsidies, the economic difficulties of the sector, and the EU policies on agriculture and livestock.

On 15 April 2022, private transport drivers working in the tourism sector rallied in Matera (Matera, Basilicata) to protest the municipal administration's decision to change the rules of access and vehicular circulation in the locality of Murgia Timone, in the Natinal Murgia Park.

On 17 June 2020, demonstrators gathered in front of the Yara agrochemical factory in Montoir-de-Bretagne. They symbolically gave the factory the 'Pinocchio award' of the worst agrobusiness. They protested as part of a day of actions to 'refuse the re-intoxication of the world' for a fairer and more responsible world.

On 12 November 2023, half a thousand people, called by PP, held a protest in Vitoria-Gasteiz (Araba, Pais Vasco) to voice their opposition to the deal that Spain's PSOE acting prime minister, Pedro Sanchez, sealed with JuntsXCat and ERC, which also includes an amnesty pact, in the hopes of securing an additional term. A TVE journalist, PP representatives, PP and Vox parliamentarians attended the protest.

On 1 September 2024, on occasion of the World Peace Day, under the motto 'Capable of Peace, not of War', at the call of BSW, around 50 people, including former pastor Brigitte Neumeister, gathered in Halle (Saale) (Sachsen-Anhalt), to protest for peace over militarization.

On 12 March 2024, at the call of Lurzaindia, more than 150 people, including farmers and CP (ELB) affiliates, gathered outside the Court of Justice in Bayonne (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to express solidarity with four Ostia affiliates who were on trial for damaging a Bouygues agency during a demonstration in 2023. The demonstrators also protested against the planned construction of a housing estate by Bouygues in the locality, which they deemed damaging to the environment.

On 14 May 2020, those working in tourism drove buses in protest in Osijek, Croatia, demanding a moratorium on leasing due to the coronavirus. This was part of a wider European 'Honk for Hope' protest action.

On 3 October 2021, around 15 far-right rioters blitz attacked members of KEERFA during an anti-fascist rally in Neo Heraklion, Athens - North Athens. The attackers randomly punched and kicked the members of KEERFA for several minutes before running off. They also attacked 2 women who were recording the incident with their phones and smashed the tables with the anti-fascist leaflets. 4 people were injured, 1 of them was a journalist for the Workers' Solidarity newspaper. 2 members of Nazi organization ProPatria, 1 of which had a swastika tattoo and was a known anti-vaxxer, were identified and arrested.

On 4 October 2023, around 2,000 people, summoned by the Manresa Diu Prou collective, held a protest in Manresa (Barcelona, Cataluna) against the insecurity in the city and the rise in petty crimes. A counter-protest against racism of around 200 people took place nearby, with participants arguing that such protests encouraged hate speech and racism. The counter-protest was called by Caritas, Bages per a tothom and A l'Aguait.

On 23 March 2025, at the call of Last Generation, environmental activists gathered outside the restaurant of starred chef Carlo Cracco in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) and poured three bottles of tomato puree on the restaurant's veranda as part of the campaign 'The Right Price' (Il Giusto Prezzo), a protest initiative organized by Last Generation to demand more climate action as well as social and economic justice.
On 24 September 2021, at least 200 people protested in Landshut at the call of FFF to urge the government to implement concrete measures to tackle climate change.

On 27 April 2024, around half a thousand people, including farmers, held a protest in Pamplona (Navarra), against industrial and intensive agriculture and livestock, which they consider to be toxic and pollutant, and demanded a change of model focused on food sovereignty.

On 27 February 2023, more than 100 people, including members of the 'Movement of solidarity with Iranians' and a PLR MP, gathered at the Place des Nations in Geneva to condemn the Iranian regime, express support for the ongoing protest movement in Iran following the death of Mahsa Amini, and demonstrate against the participation of Hossein Amir-Abdollahian, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Iran, in a simultaneous UN forum.

On 6 September 2023, during the night, citizens protested in Heraklion port for a second day over the drowning of a tardy passenger trying to board an island ferry to Heraklion at the port of Piraeus. Members of the crew were pushing the man away and one of them pushed him into the sea as the ferry was departing. The protesters, who were organized on social media, blocked the entry to the ferry sailing to Piraeus, which departed with a 6-hour delay.

On 11 May 2025, around 250 people gathered at the Hafenspitze in Flensburg (Schlweswig-Holstein) at the call of a broad coalition of civil society organizations to protest against far-right ideology and activity and to call for a ban on the AfD. The protest was part of a nationwide day of action demanding a ban on the AfD, following the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution's decision to classify the party as a 'confirmed right-wing extremist'.

On 28 November 2021, around 500 employees of the Carrefour group demonstrated in front of the supermarket in Vitrolles at the call of the CGT union. They denounced the decision of the group to put its stores under a management lease contract which would have consequences on the social rights of employees.
On 15 August 2022, residents held a protest in front of the Gijon Bullring in Gijon (Asturias) in favor of the return of the bulls to the city. The protest was summoned by Pena Taurina Gijona.

On 10 March 2020, Trieste Prison inmates hit the cells' bars to demonstrate against the measures imposed to contain the spread of coronavirus, including restrictions on family visits. The police intervened to quell the protest.

On 2 May 2021, in the afternoon, at the call of local associations and departmental council members, several hundred people demonstrated in Etampes (Ile-de-France) to protest the planned creation of a disposal site for inert dredge spoils in the commune of Saint-Hilaire. Protesters raised concerns over potential environmental degradation, water pollution, and the unsuitability of the local road network for heavy truck traffic.

On 27 November 2021, around 400 people, among them No Vax activists, gathered in Udine to protest against the coronavirus 'green pass' restrictions. 'Costituzione in Azione' (Constitution in Action) organized the demonstration.

On 30 September 2020, around 60 members of the Platform for People Affected by Mortgages (PAH) gathered in Manresa (Barcelona) to complain about the bureaucratic obstacles for registering at the local municipality.

On 3 January 2024, striking NHS junior doctors represented by BMA picketed outside the Broomfield Hospital in Broomfield (England) over a pay dispute and working conditions. The event was part of a national industrial action.

On 3 January 2022, supporters of the Ecological Uprising movement in Serbia blocked the road with their bodies in Novi Sad as a sign of protest against the building of the Rio Tinto lithium mine in the country due to environmental concers.
On 20 January 2022, around 100 No Tav activists gathered in Trento (Trento, Trentino-Alto Adige) against the preliminary works of the Trento railway ring road.
On 6 April 2022, a group of police officers gathered in Brescia (Brescia, Lombardia) to denounce their precarious working conditions and unpaid salaries.

On 1 February 2022, around 20 health workers and professionals of the medico-social sector demonstrated in Auch, at the call of 6 unions (CFE-CGC, CGT, FSU, SUD, CNT, FO). They denounced their working conditions and called for an increase of their salaries.

On 12 December 2022, healthcare workers held a protest before the Donostia Hospital in San Sebastian (Gipuzkoa, Pais Vasco) against the deterioration of the health center and to demand for more resources.
On 25 July 2019, a group of war veterans protested in the Serbian city Nis, demanding their social security and health insurance issues be resolved.
On 14 March 2021, Animal Save activists held a vigil in Kristianstad to oppose animal rights' violations and to promote animal welfare.

On 8 June 2020, people gathered at Pittville Park in Cheltenham for a Black Lives Matter protest, demonstrating against police brutality after the killing of an unarmed black man by a police officer in the United States.

On 20 April 2024, at the call of AFPS, PCF, and LFI, around 100 people demonstrated in Ales (Occitanie) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemn the Israeli military offensive in Gaza, and demand a ceasefire.

On 14 October 2021, students and representatives of local municipalities gathered in Sant'Anna di Stazzema (Lucca, Toscana) to protest against fascism and denounce the attack on CGIL headquarters in Rome, on 9 October 2021, during a demonstration against coronavirus restrictions.
On 6 February 2023, members of ALG blocked a road in Freiburg im Breisgau to call for climate protection.
On 22 February 2025, citizens gathered in Zabalj, demanding accountability for the loss of 15 lives following the collapse of a concrete canopy at the Novi Sad railway station.

On 5 October 2023, more than 1000 demonstrators, mostly students, demonstrated in Helsinki to oppose the government's proposed cuts to services that could affect students' welfare. Activists protested against planned cuts to housing allowances, a freeze on the indexation of student grants and increases in tuition fees for non-EU/EEA students.

On 31 March 2021, around 50 retirees demonstrated in Carhaix-Plouger at the call of the CGT union, the PCF and the NPA. They called for an improved purchasing power and demanded to be vaccinated against coronavirus.
On 17 June 2021, hospitality employees and Unite the Union members protested outside the Premier Inn hotel on George Street, Glasgow, as part of a campaign for better pay.

On 21 July 2023, at the call of The Greens, people, including councilors, members of The Greens, SPD, Pulse for Stuttgart, and The Left, as well as representatives of Christian churches, migrant, and social associations, demonstrated in Stuttgart to denounce the recent shift in the city's refugee policy, and notably the CDU party's role in this change, limiting access to new housing units for refugees. They called on the city to show solidarity and provide good housing for refugees.

On 4 January 2025, hundreds of people gathered in Malatesta Square in Roma - Prenestino-Centocelle (Lazio) to protest against homophobic attacks, following an attack on two boys in Pigneto on 1 January [coded separately]. Protesters held banners reading 'We shout it with our hearts. Rights now'.
On 3 February 2024, around 60 locals, led by MAN party, protested in Bubuieci, condemning the decision of the central electoral commission to cancel the local elections results.
On 1 August 2020, around 60 members of the far right staged a protest in Dortmund. The reason for the protest was not reported.
On 24 November 2023, people gathered inside Gare du Nord in Paris (Ile-de-France) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people amid the 2023 Israel-Hamas War.
On 7 June 2020, around 150 people protested in Frankfurt am Main against a railroad crossing at which a girl died a month earlier.
On 22 January 2022, at the call of ecologist groups, nearly 400 persons demonstrated in Amiens to raise awareness about the environmental and social consequences of global warming.

On 17 November 2024, more than 12,000 (across 8 events) people, called by White Tide, held a protest in Jaen (Andalucia). The event was part of a nationwide series of demonstrations in defense of public health care, against the growing deterioration of public health, especially in primary care, and to demand measures against the increase in waiting lists and that the privatization processes stop.

On 3 August 2020, people staged a protest demonstration across Zeeland to include the Naestved area to oppose the ongoing construction of the Baltic Pipe gas pipeline. Many people blocked construction machines at the construction site and chained themselves to the machines while others staged a protest march in the town. Police personnel later removed from the site those who blocked the construction machines.

On 18 May 2020, around 30 citizens marched to protest in Pamplona by banging pots against the management of the coronavirus crisis by the Government. Protesters also called for the Government to resign.

On 13 February 2022, activists, including students, gathered for a rally in Warsaw, protesting against a proposed legal reform of school. According to them, such a law will give the conservative government too strong influence on curricula and education.

On 7 November 2024, students occupied the Albertelli High School in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to protest against the government, the school model that the government proposes, and a system that, according to protesters, foments war, genocide, and misery throughout the world.

On 2 February 2023, about 200 farmers blocked a local road near Korczowa, demanding higher support of the state to the agricultural sector. They claim that the influx of cheaper Ukrainian grain pushes down the prices too much.

On 17 May 2023, a handful of LGBTQ+ activists assembled in front of the Maison Carree in Nimes in the context of the International Day Against Homophobia and Transphobia. They defended the rights of the LGBTQ+ community and denounced hatred toward its members.

On 12 February 2021, a group of Bologna branch USB, We Remain, Power To The People, Communist Network and PRC party affiliates took part in a sit-in outside the Emilia-Romagna Region headquarters in Bologna (Bologna, Emilia-Romagna) to call for universal access to the coronavirus vaccine as well as patent-free vaccine-related research.
On 17 December 2024, thousands of people, called by UGT and CCOO, held a protest in Vigo (Galicia) to demand urgent action for affordable housing amid rising rents and stagnant wages.
On 22 December 2021, around 60 people carrying lights demonstrated in Crailsheim against coronavirus-related measures.

On 7 March 2020, around 500 farmers and livestock owners marched by driving their tractors in Palma de Mallorca (Balearic Islands) demanding fair prices for the agricultural sector. The protest was organized by several agricultural associations such as the Agrarian Association of Young Farmers (ASAJA).

On 29 January 2020, over 300 persons manifested in front of the police station of Clermont-Ferrand. They protested at the call of CGT, FO, FSU, Solidaires, UNEF et CFE-CGC, to support union activists. They had been summoned after the mobilization against the education reform on January 18 at the Blaise Pascal High School.

On 12 October 2023, employees of the Bulgarian mining and energy sector protested in Sliven against plans to close down regional power plants in the country, part of a coal phaseout plan that they claim will leave many jobless.
On 9 May 2025, Fridays For Future activists demonstrated in Linkoping, Ostergotland, to draw attention to environmental issues and to demand action against climate change.

On 21 March 2025, at the call of USB, striking call center workers employed by Assocontact staged a picket outside the headquarters of Confcommercio in Taranto (Puglia) to protest against their working conditions, the new contract proposed to workers, the wage and benefits reduction the new deal entails, and the practice of contractual dumping.
On 25 June 2021, around 250 young persons gathered at the port of Vannes on the occasion of a project X event. They threw glass bottles at the police who made an arrest.
On 11 November 2023, people staged a protest in Bermillo de Sayago (Zamora, Castilla y Leon), demanding better healthcare services.

On 9 February 2024, farmers with about 100 vehicles gathered in Inowroclaw, protesting against what they see as a low state support to the national agriculture, including excessive bureaucracy and environmental restrictions, and against ongoing import of grains from Ukraine.

On 9 April 2025, protesters, organized by the Labor Center of Corinth, rallied peacefully over the high cost of living at the call of labor federations GSEE and ADEDY during a 24-hour nationwide general strike. Unions called for sector-wide collective labor agreements, wage increases and policy measures to ease the housing crisis and inflation pressures, among other demands.
On 14 May 2020, around 70 people staged a protest at the Van der Valk Hotel in Vught against the municipal plans to restructure the N65 highway that runs through Vught.

On 1 February 2025, citizens gathered in Bocar to show support for students who are occupying their faculties, demanding accountability for the loss of 15 lives after a concrete canopy at Novi Sad's railway station collapsed, attributing the tragic event to corruption.

On 11 May 2021, shopkeepers and restaurant operators collectively closed their shutters and gathered outside of their shops at the CremonaPo shopping center of Cremona (Cremona, Lombardia) to protest against the continued shutdown of their businesses on weekends to contain coronavirus infections and demand the revocation of the measure. The protest was organized by the ANCD-CONAD, Confcommercio, Confesercenti, Federdistribuzione, Confimprese and CNCC - 'National Council of Shopping Centers' ('Consiglio nazionale dei centri commerciali') trade unions and associations.

On 25 May 2021, Priority to School affiliates and supporters and representatives of the school branch of the CGIL trade union gathered outside the Regional School Office (USR) in Florence (Firenze, Toscana) to demand more security guarantees against coronavirus infections in schools for the next school year, including the recruitment of more school staff, the commitment to reduce class sizes and more investments in school infrastructure.

On 9 May 2021, around 600 demonstrators, including members of Attac, gathered in Clermont-Ferrand. They demanded actions to tackle the climate emergency and called for improvements in the 'Climate and Resilience' bill on global warming adopted by the French Parliament on 4 May.

On 23 September 2021, 150 teachers demonstrated in Saint-Brieuc, at the call of unions (CGT, FO, Sud, SNES-FSU). They denounced their working conditions and demanded for an increase of their emoluments.

On 10 January 2022, about 1,400 people took to the streets in Jena to denounce coronavirus-related measures. Several counter-demonstrations were organized. There were direct clashes between demonstrators and counter-demonstrators before the police intervened to split both groups.

On 22 October 2020, people, most of them FdI affiliates and including their leader, took part in a flash mob outside of Montecitorio Palace in Rome - City Center to protest against the potential introduction of a second lockdown to face coronavirus infections by the government and denounce the consequences of the public handling of the coronavirus pandemic on certain professional categories.
On 19 November 2021, citizens called by the ADICAE association protested in Zaragoza (Aragon) against the recent increases in power prices.

On 26 January 2025, following leaked cell phone calls of the last moments of the victims of the Tempe rail disaster, protesters rallied in Alexandroupoli at the call of the association of the victims' families. The protesters demanded justice and accused the government of a cover-up. This was part of a large mobilization in more than 150 nationwide and international locations with the slogan 'I Have No Oxygen', the last words of one of the victims.

On 11 May 2021, Extinction Rebellion activists demonstrated in front of the Equinor headquarters in Fornebu to demand sustainable changes from the company in order to reduce the negative impact on the environment from oil and gas production.

On 1 April 2025, at the call of FO, around 20 striking social workers from the Hamelines social and medical center gathered in Bagnols-sur-Ceze (Occitanie) to protest against what they perceived as toxic management.
On 7 August 2020, Fridays For Future activists staged a protest in Uppsala to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.
On 4 December 2021, several dozens residents held a protest sit-in in Villejuif to denounce the lack of security in their area.
On 3 June 2022, at the call of CGT, around 30 health workers at the Orpea group's elderly home (EHPAD) demonstrated in Paron to denounce the non-payment of a coronavirus-related compensation bonus.

On 9 February 2024, farmers with several dozen machines blocked a local road near Celbowo, protesting against what they see as a low state support to the national agriculture, including excessive bureaucracy and environmental restrictions, and against ongoing import of grains from Ukraine.
On 20 April 2020, rioters took part in confrontations with the police in Villepinte in response to police brutality in Villeneuve-la-Garenne during confinement controls due to the coronavirus.

On 21 February 2024, financial sector workers, called by CCOO, UGT and the FINE trade union, held a protest in Barcelona (Cataluna) to demand a salary increase in line with the sector's profits, as well as significant measures to improve their working conditions.
On 21 October 2022, Fridays for Future activists demonstrated in Kalmar to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.

On 13 November 2023, unionized truck drivers for the 7th day blocked with their vehicles the border crossing point with Ukraine in Korczowa. They were condemning allegedly unfair conditions for Ukrainian transport and trade companies and demanded stronger state oversight.

On 9 November 2024, at least 4 PETA members gathered in front of the restaurant 'Neue Mohr'sche Anlage' in Saarbrucken (Saarland) against the sale of frog legs, which they claimed involved animal cruelty.

On 16 March 2023, an unknown number of people assembled in Nimes to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution.
On 13 October 2023, Women's Strike movement activists demonstrated in Stockholm in support of women's rights and to oppose violence against women.

On 17 July 2022, the Ukrainian community of Pafos rallied at the waterfront to protest against Russia's invasion of Ukraine. They lit candles to commemorate the Ukrainians who died in the war and said Russia is committing genocide. The protesters requested the international community put more pressure on Russia.

On 28 October 2022, Zenith Service Group cleaning workers, working at the Massimo theatre in Palermo (Palermo, Sicilia), staged a demonstration at the entrance of the theatre to protest against their contractual conditions. Filcams CGIL and Fisascat CISL took part in the demonstration.
On 19 February 2022, between 40 and 50 people, in majority Ukrainians demonstrated in Bordeaux to denounce the threats of Russian invasion against Ukraine.

On 18 February 2021, about 200 people took part in a sit-in organized by the Democratic Lawyers association outside the town hall in Genova (Genova, Liguria) to protest against the Municipality's proposal to create an anti-fascist and anti-communist registry to ban their respective 'propaganda', and denounce their being put on an equal footing. The protest saw the participation of ANPI and ARCI association affiliates, CGIL and USB trade union representatives and affiliates, as well as PD, PC, PCI, PCL and PRC party officials.

On 25 September 2021, people gathered along the Serchio river in the Serchio River Park in Lucca for a demonstration in support of the hydraulic and environmental safety of the land. The event was organized in collaboration with Legambiente to mark the 'Clean the world 2021' initiative. The demonstrators cleaned the river area from waste and plastic. A regional council member and a local council member took part in the demonstration.

On 29 January 2024, farmers set up a road blockade on the D931 roundabout in Nogaro (Occitanie). The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement called by FNSEA and JA against rising production costs, stricter environmental norms restricting the use of pesticides, foreign imports, and bureaucratic constraints.
On 1 November 2022, railroad employees protested in Bludenz for better pay amid ongoing wage negotiations.

On 20 September 2024, residents of local villages protested in Bjelasica, and prevented the construction works near the spring of the river Ljevaja in Kolasin where there is a plan to construct a snowmaking and water supply system for two nearby ski and tourist centers. Residents believe that this construction is harmful to the environment, and also point to unresolved property issues.

On 21 April 2020, at least 8 former staff of the Debenhams department store protested outside of the store in the Limerick city. The department store closed of all of its shops in early April without securing staff redundancy packages, which sparked protests around the country. It was supported by the Mandate trade union.
On 23 January 2020, several activists affiliated to the KOD movement gathered in Piotrkow Trybunalski near a local court, demanding real independence for the judicial sector in Poland.
On 18 June 2021, around 35 employees of the Siap-Prociner company demonstrated in Bassens. They called for equal pay for all employees of the company, regardless of the branch they work for.
On 21 July 2020, tens of artists and musicians protested outside the government building in Chisinau-Buiucani against the coronavirus restrictions on the mass events.

On 4 March 2025, in the afternoon, about 30 members of the Concerted Action Territory (Territoire d'Action Concertee - TAC) association, alongside the mayor of Clohars-Carnoet (political affiliation not specified), gathered outside the Festival Hall in Clohars-Carnoet (Bretagne) to protest against the Milin Polan wind farm project, led by the company Quenea, due to concerns over lack of public consultation, environmental impact, and potential nuisances for local residents.

On 8 January 2024, farmers staged a protest with their tractors in Wittenberg (Sachsen-Anhalt), as part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement against the German government's agricultural policies, notably its plans to introduce budget cuts to Agrardiesel and remove vehicle tax exemptions.
On 1 January 2021, a protest against the government was held in Ljubljana, Slovenia.
On 18 May 2021, around 25 people, among them AFD members and supporters, protested in Krailling, Munchen, ahead of a council session against a planned wind park in the area.
On 10 February 2019, approximately 70 persons with disabilities and their assistants protested outside the Mures prefecture, demanding corresponding allocations in the new 2019 budget law.
On 21 April 2021, shopkeepers and business owners protested in Ayia Napa demanding immediate financial support by the government due to the coronavirus pandemic.

On 16 July 2021, De Angeli Institute workers gathered outside their company in Reggello (Firenze, Toscana) to demand guarantees on the future of the company. Filctem CGIL and RSU took part in the demonstration.
On 23 February 2025, several hundred activists gathered in Wroclaw for a rally in front of the local consulate of Ukraine, protesting against the presence of the so-called Azov battalion in the city.
On 18 October 2022, KOD activists gathered for a rally in Katowice, protesting against alleged politicization of courts in Poland.

On 25 January 2024, farmers who left from neighboring localities drove at a slow pace to protest on the N158 road, before converging and gathering in Caen (Normandie). The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement called by FNSEA and JA against rising production costs, stricter environmental norms restricting the use of pesticides, foreign imports, and bureaucratic constraints.

On 9 April 2024, at the call of Changing Course, students, teachers, and researchers demonstrated outside the Politecnico University in Milano - Municipio 3 (Lombardia) against the collaboration of Italian and Israeli universities and the so-called MAECI call of cooperation. A group of students also interrupted the meeting of the university rectorate to express their concerns and demand the university to take a stance in favor of Palestinians. Representatives of Power to the People were present.

On 31 January 2022, around 50 women and their supporters gathered in Newport to protest the arrest of a 53-year-old local women 'on suspicion of criminal damage and displaying threatening or abusive writing likely to cause harassment, alarm or distress'. Protesters heard from representatives from Women's Rights Network and Standing for Women. Protesters expressed pro-feminist and anti-police sentiments.

On 20 March 2024, parents and school support staff of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) represented by GMB held a protest outside the Civic Hall in Leeds (England) to call on authorities to improve their special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) service.

On 14 March 2021, 16 people, dressed as lawyers, staged a protest in Dendermonde in the context of the nationwide climate protest action Lawyers for the Climate to demand a more ambitious climate policy.

On 6 April 2023, at noon, people gathered at Colbert square and headed towards the harbor master's office in Rochefort. The event was part of an eleventh national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FAGE, FIDL, and MNL) to oppose the passing of a pension reform bill by means of Article 49.3 of the constitution by the government, and call for the withdrawal of the bill.

On 6 October 2023, FFF activists took to the streets in Bologna (Bologna, Emilia-Romagna) to call for more climate action and social justice under the framework of Fridays for Future's Global Climate Strike.

On 11 January 2024, people, including farmers and Chairwoman of the Wetterau-Frankfurt Regional Farmers' Association, Andrea Rahn-Farr, with a total of 2,000 (according to the organizers) or more than 600 tractors (according to the police), gathered in Frankfurt am Main (Hessen), some reaching it as convoys from across the region, to demonstrate. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement against planned agricultural subsidy cuts.

On 23 May 2024, at the call of SNES-FSU, teachers gathered outside the local school in Ducey-les-Cheris (Normandie) to oppose the government's education reform, especially the introduction of level groups for students, and demand more state funding for public schools.

On 1 October 2021, around 250 people demonstrated in Montbeliard, at the call of 9 unions (CGT, FO, SUD, FSU, CGC, CFTC, UNRPA-Ensemble et Solidaires, FGR, LSR). They called for an increase of their pensions.
On 22 December 2018, passengers of a train blocked the railway in Bucharest's Gara de Nord, protesting the overcrowded railcars.

On 19 November 2024, at the call of CGIL and FILT CGIL, striking AMAT workers held a picket outside the Prefecture in Palermo (Sicilia), demanding improved working conditions and the renewal of their national collective labor agreement. They condemned delays in adopting a new industrial plan and service contract, which they deemed essential for addressing staff shortages and enhancing their work environment.

On 2 March 2022, kindergarten children gathered outside the town hall in Somma Lombardo (Varese, Lombardia) to call for peace and condemn the war after the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine. The Mayor and kindergarten teachers took part in the demonstration.

On 10 January 2022, students from middle schools, elementary schools, and various high schools including Sannazaro, Vittorini and Caro in Napoli (Napoli, Campania), staged a demonstration against the reopening of schools with in-presence classes without safer studying conditions amid a spike in the coronavirus cases, as it is not possible to keep physical distance among students. But they also were opposed to online classes as the conditions for access are not provided by the government nor considered an adequate solution to children's welfare.
On 25 January 2024, XR activists gathered outside Havas Media UK offices in London - Camden (England) over companies partnership with Shell company.
On 18 December 2021, people, led by MHM members, protested in Veszprem against the coronavirus vaccination mandate.

On 10 November 2022, a group of people gathered in Palermo (Palermo, Sicilia) in support of the citizens' income. Demonstrators collected signatures of bystanders and displayed a banner. University students took part in the event.
On 1 March 2021, around 350 Syntegon Technology GmbH employees protested in Crailsheim for higher wages amidst collective wage negotiations. The protest was organized by the IGM.
On 27 June 2020, hundreds of vehicles took part in a protest procession in Strumica against the opening of a mine, alleging irregularities on behalf of its investors.
On 14 March 2023, at the call of Ver.di union, around 200 striking municipal employees demonstrated in Laupheim to call for higher wages in the public sector.
On 18 August 2020, around 100 people protested in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf (Berlin) for more environmental protection.

On 7 December 2024, at the call of CAAR - Anti-Racist Counter-Attack Collective (Collectif Contre-Attaque Anti-Raciste), more than 60 people gathered in Grasse (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to support a woman named Carolle and her family, who claim to have endured years of racism from their neighbors, and raise awareness on the persistence of racism and demand justice.

On 26 August 2021, Alitalia airline company workers, including flight attendants, gathered outside the company's former headquarters in Rome - Europa (Roma, Lazio) to demand guarantees for their professional future following the reorganization of Alitalia as ITA.
On 18 January 2021, Querdenken supporters protested in Milbertshofen, Munchen, against the coronavirus protection measures.

On 15 January 2024, around 200 farmers drove their vehicles in Sibiu in protest of the high insurance fees, the high fuel price, and the high taxes. The protesters also demanded a stop to the import of cereals and a review of the agricultural subsidies.
On Nov. 5, 2018: Poultry-farmers protested in Sofia against bird flu measures, which they deemed to be extreme and detrimental to their business.
On 26 July 2020, around 500 members of the LGBT community protested in Leipzig for their rights under the motto 'The Future is Intersectional - Queer Perspectives'.

On 30 January 2024, at the call of Farmers of Lower Saxony (Landvolk Niedersachsen), farmers with 40 vehicles drove, with the support of local small- and medium-sized businesses, from Holger Meier dairy farm in Deelsen (Niedersachsen) to the town hall in Kirchlinteln (Niedersachsen), to demonstrate against the planned increase in agricultural taxes in their locality. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement against several agricultural policies of the federal government, including planned agricultural subsidy cuts.
On 8 March 2024, on the occasion of International Women's Day, people, including SNES-FSU affiliates, gathered in Bar-le-Duc (Grand Est) to demonstrate in favor of women's rights and equal pay.

On 15 October 2021, in the morning, Electrolux workers gathered, with the support of RSU union representatives, outside their company's gates in Susegana (Treviso, Veneto) to protest against the extension of coronavirus 'green pass' restrictions to public and private sector workers, set to come into force on that day. Vaccinated workers reportedly took part in the protest to express solidarity with their colleagues.
On 12 January 2024, Fridays For Future activists demonstrated in Malmo, Skane, to draw attention to environmental issues and to demand action against climate change.

On 17 March 2022, transport workers cut the road traffic and formed a picket line in Lugo (Galicia), demanding better working conditions and complaining about the high fuel prices. The Platform for the Defense of the Freight Transport Sector called a nationwide strike action.

On 16 May 2020, people came together in Siena (Siena, Toscana) on the occasion of a protest organized by the Tricolor Masks movement against the Italian government and its management of the coronavirus crisis. Media reported that similar protests occurred all around Italy.

On 7 September 2022, around 200 people, including women, employees of the maternity ward and midwives demonstrated in Henstedt-Ulzburg against the closure of obstetrics and gynecology at the Paracelsus Clinic. Many local and state politicians also attended, including Alveslohe's Mayor.

On 18 April 2021, citizens protested in the railway station of Selgua (Huesca), demanding to resume the train services suspended due to the outbreak of the coronavirus pandemic. The Aragonese platform 'Don't lose your train' called the protest.
On 28 May 2020, around thirty homeless people (Italians and foreigners) gathered in Padua to ask for a better accommodation compared with the one provided during the coronavirus emergency.

On 28 August 2024, a group of protesters gathered in Witten (Nordrhein-Westfalen), to protest against the AfD's political activities, which included an information stand outside of the election campaign period. The demonstration was organized in response to the AfD's presence and activities, reflecting local discontent with the party's political stance.

On 24 June 2023, between 3,500 and 5,000 people, including the LGBTQ+ community, demonstrated at the Rathausplatz to Schauspielhaus and at Dr.-Ruer-Platz in Bochum against the injustices and violence that queer people face. They gathered on the occasion of Christopher Street Day (CSD).

On 13 August 2022, at the call of S.I. COBAS, security and reception workers of Eurospin supermarkets held a protest in Parma (Parma, Emilia-Romagna) to demand a wage increase and regularization of part-time contracts, sickness and leave policies.

On 16 October 2023, at the call of several unspecified teachers' unions, around 100 people, including teachers, gathered in front of the town hall in Gueret (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to pay tribute to the teacher who was killed in an Islamist terror attack on 13 October 2023 at a high school in Arras, and demonstrate against violence at school.
On 16 December 2020, students protested outside of the Ministry of Education in Tirana, demanding the resignation of Minister Kushi over his recent comments about young people.

On 12 December 2023, striking teachers, including SNES-FSU affiliates, gathered outside the Monge school in Savigny-sur-Orge (Ile-de-France). The event was part of a national day of strike and demonstration of teachers called by SNUEP-FSU, CGT Educ'Action, SNETAA-FO, SUD Education, SNALC, as well as other teaching unions, to demonstrate against the vocational school reform, which they deemed ill-adapted to students' needs and detrimental to the quality of their training.

On 2 July 2022, around 150 demonstrators, including members of feminist groups, gathered in Rouen. They called for the fundamental right to abortion for women after the US Supreme Court decided to revoke it.
On 5 November 2021, around 300 FFF members protested in Bonn for climate justice and to put pressure on the governments attending the COP26 World Climate Conference in Glasgow.

On 4 November 2019, residents of Chios blocked symbolically the road leading to VIAL, the island's reception facility hosting some 5,000 migrants near the village of Chalkeio, to protest the camp's growing population that is several times above its maximum capacity.
On 1 March 2019, several judges and prosecutors protested outside the Botosani Justice Palace against a governmental decree limiting judicial independence.
On 2 October 2021, dozens of residents marched through Derby city center in protest against knife-related violence. This event was part of the 'Walk Against Knife Crime' campaign.

On 14 May 2024, around 100 people, including members of the Jewish community, gathered outside the 'Mur des Justes' monument in Paris (Ile-de-France) to condemn antisemitism after red hands were painted on the monument a few hours earlier.
On 9 April 2022, around 200 persons demonstrated in Reims at the call of ANV-Cop 21, Nous Toutes and SOS Racism. They called for a better future and for measures against the climate emergency.

On 14 April 2024, dozens of residents of the Pazardzhik villages of Patalenitsa, Vetren dol and Varvara joined a protest against prepared amendments to the Environmental Protection Act, claiming the new changes remove the influence and oversight of experts and relevant environmental agencies for construction and investment projects that could be damaging for the environment.

On 27 March 2023, hundreds of people gathered outside the House of Commons in London - Westminster to protest against the Government's Illegal Migration Bill. SUTR organized the protest, and Labour MPs Jeremy Corbyn and Dawn Butler addressed the crowd alongside representatives from PCS, Unite, Unison, TSSA, Care4Calais, the Jewish Socialist Group, and the Stop the War Coalition.
On 20 January 2022, several hundred people demonstrated in Moss to oppose rising electricity prices in the country.

On Feb. 9 2019, in an escalation of the countrywide farmers' mobilisations since Jan. 28, farmers at the junction of Derveni blocked traffic on both lanes of the Kavala-Thessaloniki highway allowing only emergency cases to drive through. They are mainly protesting against high energy and production costs and high taxation.

On 17 May 2020, a group of people marched to protest in Getafe (Madrid) by banging pots against the management of the coronavirus crisis by the Government. Protesters also called for the Government to resign.

On 5 July 2019, residents of Mammari and the surrounding area in the outskirts of Nicosia protested against the 'unbearable smell' of livestock and chicken farms in close proximity to their homes. Representatives of political parties AKEL and DISY were present at the protest.

On 22 March 2024, 200 farmers with around 20 tractors, called by ASAJA, participated in a motorcade through the streets of Valladolid (Castilla y Leon), to demonstrate. Farmers demanded the elimination of penalties for the use of water resources in irrigated farms and the development of a new Hydrological Plan.

On 29 May 2021, Belarusian activists gathered for a rally in Biala Podlaska, declaring their solidarity with the political opposition at home and demanding immediate release of journalist Protasevich, who was arrested in Minsk.

On 28 February 2025, at the call of Film, Fiom, and UIL, metalworkers gathered outside the headquarters of Confindustria Basilicata in Potenza (Calabria) to demand the renewal of the national collective labor agreement for metalworkers.
On 5 January 2022, around 100 delivery riders on motorcycles staged a ride protest in Bristol to demand more protection from violence and harassment they suffered while working.
On 11 February 2021, ITP Aero workers, a company in the aeronautical engines market, gathered in Barakaldo (Bizkaia) to protest against dismissal proceedings affecting many employees.
On 12 December 2020, around 80 persons demonstrated in Clichy. They called for decent housing for undocumented families, housed by the city council in unsanitary hotels.

On 15 January 2020, between 16 and 22 Extinction Rebellion activists protested at the Landtag in Dusseldorf for more action against climate change and glued themselves to the windows and walls of the building. Police dispersed the protest and un-glued several protesters.
On 4 June 2023, activists from the Animal Alliance demonstrated in Odense to oppose animal agriculture, to promote animal welfare and plant-based diet.

On 30 January 2024, farmers with around 200 tractors staged a protest on the A81 highway near Sulz am Neckar (Baden-Wurttemberg), disrupting traffic. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement against several agricultural policies of the federal government, including planned agricultural subsidy cuts.

On 26 January 2025, following leaked cell phone calls of the last moments of the victims of the Tempe rail disaster, protesters rallied in Ios at the call of the association of the victims' families. The protesters demanded justice and accused the government of a cover-up. This was part of a large mobilization in more than 150 nationwide and international locations with the slogan 'I Have No Oxygen', the last words of one of the victims.

On 11 December 2024, public employees, called by CCOO, UGT, ANPE, USO, the Federation of Associations of Education Inspectors and Inspecting Officers (Federacion de Asociaciones de Inspectores e Inspectoras de Educacion - ADIDE), the Union of Education Inspectors (Union Sindical de Inspectores de Educacion - USIE), the Federal Police Union (Union Federal de Policia - UFP), ACAIP, and the Independent Union of the Tax Agency (Sindicato Independiente de la Agencia Tributaria - SIAT), held a protest outside Muface offices in Ourense (Galicia) to defend Muface, a mutual healthcare system, against potential integration into the public health system.
On 15 February 2021, around 30 parents of students from five schools gathered in Macerata to protest against the municipality's decision to reorganize the canteen system.

On 10 January 2022, dozens of farmers protested in Zwolle (Overijssel) while a request brought by Farmers Defence Force was being discussed by a provincial commission. A year earlier, Farmers Defense Force had filed an enforcement request against the Jumbo distribution center in Raalte requesting that Jumbo also needed a Nature Conservation Permit to operate near a Natura 2000 area, just as farmers must have one.

On 4 November 2023, at 2 pm, at the call of Alliance for Peace (Bundnis fur Frieden) which includes BPD, Reich Citizens, Freedom Parade, Radio Dawn (Radio Morgenrote), and Fumigation for Mother Earth (Rauchern fur Mutter Erde), almost 250 people demonstrated in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) under the motto 'Peace now'. Grannies Against the Right and Straight Thinking (Geradedenken) members gathered for a counter-demonstration at the Jewish cemetery to denounce the demonstration's links with far-right movements and conspiracy ideologies.
On 13 January 2022, around 100 unionized teachers protested in Victory's Square in Bucharest, demanding higher salaries and more investment in the education.

On 3 April 2023, members of ALG demonstrated and disrupted an SPD event in Lohbrugge in Hamburg - Bergedorf to call for climate protection. The people in the event loudly protested against climate protests. An elderly man stormed the stage and tried to reach the mayor. Bodyguards pushed him away, and police officers arrested him.

On 9 March 2024, farmers continued blocking the border crossing point near Dorohusk, protesting against ongoing import of Ukrainian grains into the EU and against restrictions related to the so-called Green Deal.

On 7 September 2019, several hundred people in Valjevo, Serbia, protested over a gathering which was supposed to show support for the upcoming Belgrade Pride march. The original gathering was then cancelled.
On 10 July 2021, around 80 retail workers protested in Heilbronn at the call of Ver.di for higher salaries amid collective wage negotiations.

On 14 May 2021, Ilva steel factory workers from Taranto and trade unionists initiated, at the call of FIOM CGIL and UILM, a march outside the Ministry of Economic Development in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to call for the ecological reconversion of the factory and urge national authorities to find a settlement to the issue.

On 23 November 2022, citizens, summoned by CSIF, held a protest in Malaga (Andalucia) to demand quality public services and denounce deficiencies in health, education, justice, and the Andalusian government.

On 22 July 2021, GKN Driveline automotive workers received the visit and support of FNSI and other journalist trade unions' officials and affiliates while picketing outside their factory in Campi Bisenzio (Firenze, Toscana) to protest against the announced closure of the plant and the resultant dismissal of its 422 workers.

On 14 November 2024, at the call of CGT, striking GMD employees gathered for a picket line outside their workplace in La Souterraine (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to demand more transparency on their factory's financial status and safe jobs.

On 15 May 2021, around 120 people protested in Wurzburg in solidarity with Palestinians amid escalating tensions in the Middle East between Palestine and Israel. Three people gathered for a counterprotest, carrying an Israeli flag. The report mentions a hassle between both groups. It is not clear if it was a verbal hassle or if there was a physical interaction.

On 17 January 2023, several dozen farmers affiliated with Solidarity gathered in in Slupsk, protesting against import of the Ukrainian products into Poland, because it allegedly harms the domestic agricultural market.
On 20 March 2021, around 50 environmental activists protested in Bernay to call on the government to implement concrete measures to tackle climate change.

On 15 November 2023, about 1,000 employees of the public sector participated in a protest in Hannover (Region Hannover, Niedersachsen) called for by Ver.di in the context of wage negotiations in the public sector of Federal States.

On 25 May 2024, an unknown number of XR activists protested in Tilburg (Noord-Brabant) to denounce fast fashion and its impact on life and the planet. The event took place as part of a Guerilla Fashion Week throughout the Netherlands.

Around 15 May 2021 (as reported), people, among them Torino Tricolore activists, gathered in the Borgo Vittoria area of Torino to protest against drug dealing and demand the redevelopment of the area.

On 25 July 2019, residents of the Aerodrom Municipality in Skopje held a peaceful protest in front of a clinic against the government's decision to treat addicts at this local clinic, fearing the safety of their children.
On 16 November 2021, around 10 nurse anesthetists slowed down the traffic in Brest at the call of CGT to demand the recognition of their specialized profession and better salaries.
On 9 October 2020, parents protested in Ludwigshafen am Rhein against the compulsory wearing of face masks against the coronavirus.
On 20 June 2020, health workers gathered in Malaga to claim for a better public health scheme. Protestors demanded more material and economic resources amid coronavirus pandemic.
On 14 March 2022, farmers gathered in La Puebla de Hijar (Teruel) complaining about the high fuel prices.
