On 13 April 2021, trade union activists gathered in front of the Korsor Hospital in Korsor demanding to improve the working conditions of construction workers engaged in the renovation of the hospital and accusing the contractor company of violating workers' rights.

On 4 July 2020, Stop Islamisation of Norway protested outside the Storting Parliament in Oslo. They were met by a group of counter-protesters. Two people were arrested and two people expelled from the protest due to 'minor issues'.

On 16 February 2023, between 80 ([according to] police) and 200 ([according to] unions) people gathered for a protest in Louhans. The event was part of a fifth national and cross-sector day of strike and protest called by the CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform.

On 10 May 2023, about 50 No Vax and No Green Pass activists gathered in protest outside the courthouse in Brescia (Brescia, Lombardia) against the policies adopted during the coronavirus pandemic, on the occasion of the hearing of former the Italian president and former minister of Health in the context of the coronavirus trial.

On 21 November 2020, nearly 500 people, including yellow vests demonstrators and small business owners, demonstrated in Nancy to condemn the government's management of the coronavirus health crisis as disastrous. They demonstrated against the implementation of a national security bill as well as to denounce police violence. Police used tear gas to disperse demonstrators who retaliated by throwing projectiles. One man was injured and had to go to the hospital after the police intervention. 5 police officers were injured as well.

On 27 August 2022, between 250 and 300 anti-speciesist activists marched from the main train station to the city of Lausanne. They called for an end to speciesism and the premise that man is superior to animals. They also called for the closure of slaughterhouses and the recognition of the rights of animals.

On 22 January 2022, hundreds of anti-vaccination protesters gathered in Cardiff to show opposition to the government-led coronavirus vaccine roll-out. Protesters criticised the government for floating rules set in place as part of its effort to reduce the spread of coronaviurs.

On 28 September 2024, at the call of PP, around 70 people, including Venezuelan nationals, members of the Venezuelan community as well as PP mayor, provincial president, national and regional deputies, held a protest in Vilagarcia de Arousa (Galicia) in support of Edmundo Gonzalez, arguing he was the rightful winner of the results of the 28 July 2024 general elections in Venezuela, which they denounced as an 'electoral fraud' by Nicolas Maduro. They demanded a fair process, as well as the revision of the electoral records.

On 7 February 2023, around 7,000 people staged a protest in Morlaix. The event was part of a third national and cross-sector day of strike and protest called by CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform.

On 22 March 2025, at the call of a former AfD politician, under the motto 'For Law and Order. Against far-left extremism and Politically motivated Violence', around 850 people gathered in Berlin - Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg (Berlin) to demand stricter law enforcement. Over 2,000 participated in 15 counter-demonstrations against the far-right event, blocking streets with both sides shoving and pushing each other in attempts to advance or block the march. The counter-demonstrators broke through police lines, which led to the police using pepper spray against them. Some individuals from the far-right group committed acts of bodily harm to counter-demonstrators, leading to around 100 arrests. Counter-demonstrators faced over 20 arrests for resistance. The event was part of a broader far-right mobilization against immigration, government policies, and support for Ukraine.

On 30 March 2023, around 50 people, including CP, CGT, SUD, LFI, and Attac members, gathered in front of the Sub-Prefecture in Draguignan to denounce police violence during the SLT demonstration in Sainte-Soline on 25 March 2023. The event was part of a national day of protest called by SLT to denounce police violence and oppose plans by the Interior Ministry to shut down the association.

On 4 June 2022, an unknown number of activists of Vlaams Belang and Rassemblement National staged a joint protest in De Panne against the imminent establishment of 46 300-meter-high wind turbines off the coast of De Panne by the French authorities.

On 22 December 2023, at the call of CGIL, CSIL, and UIL, and under the framework of a national strike, about 400 workers employed in the so-called third sector, which includes commerce, catering, tourism, and large-scale distribution protested in Cagliari (Sardegna) to protest against their working conditions and demand increase in wages. Protesters also demanded the renewal and update of the sector's national labor contract.
On 2 March 2022, people gathered in Eskilstuna to denounce the Russian invasion of Ukraine and call on authorities to promote peace.

On 4 May 2021, temporary workers and employees of the entertainment and cultural industries, continued the occupation of a theater in Le Havre. They protested against the forced closure of the arts sector due to coronavirus-related measures implemented by the government and against unemployment benefit reforms.

On 11 July 2020, people gathered in Palermo (Palermo, Sicily) under the banner 'Let's Remain Free' to protest against a draft law against homotransphobia. Protesters claimed that such a law would affect their freedom of expression, education, religion, social and political aggregation.

On 14 April 2025, protesting doctors from the capital's St. Catherine Hospital in Sofia demanded a 20 percent increase in their salaries after weeks of protest and a lack of response from institutions. They claim that a lack of decent pay is discouraging doctors and the lack of pay for overtime violates basic labor rights.

On 6 August 2022, a few anti-nuclear activists, including members of MLPD and IB, protested in Munchen to call for the government to abolish nuclear weapons and nuclear energy. Demonstrators were against the war in Ukraine, imperialism, militarization, environmental catastrophes, and the prospect of a nuclear third world war. They had gathered on the occasion of the 77th anniversary of the Hiroshima and Nagasaki nuclear bombings in Japan.

On 30 April 2021, restaurant and bar operators, market vendors and retailers pitched tents across Italia square for the third consecutive day in Sassari (Sassari, Sardegna) to protest against anti-coronavirus measures recently adopted by the national government, notably regarding closing and opening times. The protest, whereby participants asked for greater help measures from authorities, was organized by the 'Tents on the Square' ('Tende in piazza') spontaneous committee.
On 24 September 2021, people protested in Steyr-Stadt at the call of FFF to urge the government to implement concrete measures to tackle climate change.

Around 29 July 2023 (as reported), hundreds of citizen's income recipients gathered in front of the INPS (national institute for social security) headquarters in De Gasperi street in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to protest against the abolishment of the country's citizen's income starting in August for households that do not include people with disabilities, minors or members over 60 and are therefore deemed employable.

On 27 March 2025, five people demonstrated in Christiania, Copenhagen, to oppose the Danish government's proposal to allow permanent US military bases on Danish soil and to express their dissatisfaction with US President Donald Trump's policies.
On 21 February 2022, around 500 people, including far-right members, demonstrated in Halberstadt against coronavirus-related measures.
On 13 October 2022, hundreds of people, including Jean-Luc Melenchon, held a rally in front of the town hall in Paris in solidarity with refinery workers on strike over pay amid inflation.

On 13 June 2020, over 300 demonstrators gathered in front of the US Embassy in Stockholm for a Black Lives Matter protest against racism and police violence. Later, police forces dispersed the protest as it exceeded the maximum number of 50 participants.

On 20 October 2022, inmates in the prison house in Velletri (Roma, Lazio) barricaded themselves in the common areas from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. because they did not want to return to their prison cells for unreported reasons. Prison guards transferred the protesters to another prison house.

On 8 March 2025, people demonstrated in Skelleftea, Vasterbotten, to mark International Women's Day. Activists from an Extinction Rebellion associated group highlighted the urgency of protecting future generations from climate change and to environmental issues.
On 15 November 2021, nurse anesthetists gathered outside the Regional Health Agency in Saint-Brieuc to demand the recognition of their specialized profession and better salaries.

On 26 December 2022, between 450 and 1,000 people, including members of the Kurdish community, PCF, MP and feminist groups, demonstrated in Rennes to denounce the killing of 3 Kurdish activists in Paris on 23 December by a 69-year-old man with racist motives.

On 15 September 2022, residents, summoned by CCOO, held a protest in Albacete (Castilla-La Mancha) against sexist violence and crimes against women within the framework of the Equality Day at the Albacete Fair.

On 20 June 2020, around 1000 persons gathered, in Granadilla de Abona (Santa Cruz de Tenerife), in support of the two environmental activists who climbed the cranes used for the construction of a hotel on the waterfront on the beach of La Tejita. The activists together with protesters demanded the stoppage of the construction project.

On 23 January 2025, during farmers' mobilizations over rising production costs and inadequate infrastructure among other issues, the farmers of Trikala rolled out their tractors and other vehicles at the Megalochori junction, where they set up a roadblock at the call of the Federation of Farmers' Associations 'The Spring'. The leader of the Federation made statements.

On 26 November 2020, around 100 school employees and CFDT union members protested in Besancon to denounce the government's management of the coronavirus health crisis. They denounced a lack of financial, material, and human resources to implement an effective health protocol in schools.

On 18 November 2021, people, including members of several organizations (MLPD, Youth League Rebel (REBELL), SI, AUF: Essen Rise Up), protested in Gelsenkirchen against European imperialism and in solidarity with asylum seekers stranded at the Polish-Belarusian border.

On 3 October 2020, around 150 activists of the Ineos Will Fall coalition staged a protest in Antwerpen by occupying the future Ineos Phenol Project One facility in the Port of Antwerp, to denounce its imminent establishment there. Police forces intervened to vacate the area and arrested all activists.

On 12 December 2022, residents staged a protest outside Our Lady's Hospital in Navan to oppose changes to ambulance protocols, which they claimed would result in more patients diverting from Navan to Drogheda.
On 30 April 2023, around 400 people staged a protest march through the old town of Heidelberg at the call of anti-fascists, to protest against right-wing fraternities in the city.
On 12 December 2021, oppositional parties, including DS and SSP organized a protest in Obrenovac, Serbia, because the city was left without heat during freezing temperatures.

On 17 July 2024, 50 people, called by an anti-eviction group, held a protest in front of a building in Girona (Cataluna) against the eviction of an 84-year-old woman whose apartment was owned by a speculation fund. Members of the local government (We Win Girona), including the mayor, took part in the protest. However, their presence was not supported by the anti-eviction group who held the protest.

On 27 January 2021, around 20 workers and employers of the hospitality industry protested in Gijon (Asturias), demanding that the regional government provide direct aids to their labor sector. Protesters complained about their difficult economic conditions caused by the coronavirus restrictions. The Hospitality with Consciousness (HCC) association called the protest.

On 10 April 2025, at the call of CGT Spectacle and the National Union of Plastic Artists (Syndicat National des Artistes Plasticiens - SNAP), around 50 artists and workers from the cultural sector gathered outside the Grand Theatre in Bordeaux (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to protest against state-imposed budget cuts for the cultural sector.

On 21 April 2025, at the call of local union delegates, around 20 striking health workers gathered outside the hospital in Bordeaux (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to demand the payment of a bonus linked to external laboratory activities. Protesters denounced what they described as mismanagement by the hospital leadership, warning that delays in biological analyses were affecting patient discharge times.

On 11 December 2020, workers of the events and shows industry gathered in Granada, representing a 'symbolical burial' to protest over the 'abandonment' and lack of support to public institutions' cultural sector. Protesters complained about their economic situation following the restrictions to prevent the spread of coronavirus infections. They demanded direct aid and decreasing municipal taxation. The protest was organized nationwide by the Red Alert movement.
On 12 May 2020, Albanian land workers, who are permanent residents in Imathia [coded to Veroia] participated in a strike-protest demanding an increase of their wages.

On 14 June 2021, around 800 persons staged several protests in Biel/Bienne as part of the Women's strike. They called for an earlier retirement age, salary raise and the protection of women against sexist and sexual violence.
On 10 January 2022, people demonstrated in Enkoping to express their support for peace and prosperity in Bosnia and Herzegovina amid rising political tensions in the country.

On 5 January 2020, almost 300 people gathered at the Clock Tower in Leicester city centre to protest against India's new Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) and National Register of Citizens (NRC), which excludes Muslims from Indian citizenship.

On 17 December 2021, around 150 Ence company workers protested in Pontevedra (Galicia), demanding the continuity of the factory located in Lourizan. They also complained about the judicial process against a unionist after a group of union affiliates enclosed themselves inside the city council to demand solutions to their situation.

On 8 June 2024, at the call of AFPS, around 100 people demonstrated in Lannion (Bretagne) to demand a ceasefire in Gaza, express solidarity with the Palestinian people, and condemn what they deemed a 'genocide' of Gazans by the Israeli army.
On 14 February 2021, an unknown number of people staged a protest in Libramont to demand more attention for children and youngsters during the coronavirus crisis.
On 26 October 2024, Fridays For Future activists demonstrated in Lidkoping, Vastra Gotaland, to draw attention to environmental issues and to demand action against climate change.

On 31 March 2021, women and their supporters gathered outside Leinster House in Dublin to call for more to be done to protect women who are facing gender violence, particularly those whose situations have been made worse by the coronavirus pandemic. This event was organized by ROSA.

On 6 August 2022, activists of the '#IamPoorAffected' demonstrated in front of the Red City Hall in Berlin - Mitte to call for support for people with low incomes in the face of rising energy and food prices, as well as inflation. Demonstrators demanded the redistribution of existing resources and were against the growing gap between the rich and poor. The event was part of a national day of protests called by the 'OneWorryLess' Foundation.
On 17 December 2021, around 60 people demonstrated in Oschatz against coronavirus-related measures.

On 29 August 2024, striking employees of the Youth Judicial Protection (PJJ) sector, including CGT members, demonstrated in Nimes (Occitanie) against a national social plan including a redundancy plan that foresaw the non-renewal of 500 contracts from 1 September 2024. This nationwide action was called by the inter-union SNPES-PJJ/FSU, CGT, UNSA SPJJ, and CFDT.
On 16 May 2021, people protested in Bucharest's University Square in solidarity with the Palestinian struggle.
On 21 September 2021, around 100 employees of Ikea protested in Burgwedel at the call of Ver.di union for better pay.

On 1 February 2025, at the call of UNEF, students gathered in Paris (Ile-de-France) to express solidarity with the students protesting against corruption in Serbia and pay tribute to all the demonstrators killed by Serbian law enforcement.

On 22 December 2023, 140 Extinction Rebellion activists blocked traffic around the entrance of the Shell company headquarters in Den Haag (Zuid-Holland) to denounce its use of fossil subsidies and its lack of communication on the climate crisis. Police forces arrested 60 people.

On 9 June 2023, an unknown number of employees of insurance companies protested in front of an insurance company in Waterloo (Wallonie), to demand higher wages in their company. Among the protesters were representatives of the labor union ABVV-FGTB.
On 24 July 2020, truck drivers protested in Berlin with truck rallies in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg against dumping wages and unfair freight prices.
Around 13 February 2021 (as reported), around 90 Antifa activists protested in Frankfurt-Bockenheim in solidarity with the fighters in Kurdistan.

On 11 February 2022, 300 people, including Yellow Vests and suspended health workers, gathered in Le Mans as part of the 'Freedom Convoy' movement heading to Paris and Brussels denouncing coronavirus restriction measures including the coronavirus 'vaccination pass' and decreasing purchasing power in France.

On 30 November 2021, around 300 health workers and professionals of the medico-social sector demonstrated in La Roche-sur-Yon at the call of the CFDT union. They called for application of the Segur agreements on the payment of the coronavirus-related bonus to all health and medico-social workers.

On 23 September 2023, around 50 people demonstrated in Chateauroux (Centre-Val de Loire). The event was part of a national day of protest against 'systemic racism and police violence, for social justice and the defense of civil liberties' called by CGT, LFI, alongside dozens of organizations and working-class neighborhood collectives, NGOs including Attac, Last Renovation, LDH, and Friends of the Earth, the NPA and EELV parties, as well as the FSU and SUD unions.
On 8 October 2022, around 150 animal rights activists demonstrated in Wurzburg to denounce the death of animals in slaughterhouses and call for their closure.

On 27 January 2024, traders from a local business center in Warsaw gathered for a rally in front of the mall, protesting against sharply rising rents. A minor skirmish with a bystander occurred, but was unrelated to the protest.

On 2 October 2021, around 100 people took part in three different demonstration marches to reach Cavicchioni Square in Albinea (Reggio nell'Emilia, Emilia-Romagna) to mark the 'March for Peace'. They demonstrated in support of fraternity and the environment. A council member took part in the event.
On 15 March 2019, about 50 young people held a school strike for climate in Sofia under the name 'Fridays for Future' to express their concern for climate change and ask government for action.
On 23 September 2022, Fridays for Future activists demonstrated in front of the Town Hall in Umea to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.

On 16 April 2020, between 50-100 workers of Glovo company, a food delivery start-up, gathered in front of one of its main offices in Madrid to denounce the cuts on the base rate per trip without prior notification to the company. Glovo workers demanded better working conditions who, besides the declaration of the state of alarm due to the coronavirus crisis outbreak, their services are considered as part of the essential activities. Police Forces intervened to identify some of the protesters.

On 17 October 2022, at the call of ANPJ, 200 judicial police officers, judges, lawyers, and magistrates held a protest in front of the police station and the courthouse in Bordeaux against the judicial police reform proposed by the Interior Ministry.

On 18 December 2021, dozens of demonstrators gathered in Lille at the call of organizations and unions, including SUD. They called for the regularization of undocumented persons and denounced racism and the living conditions of migrants around the world on the occasion of the International Migrants Day.

On 23 October 2021, around 5,000 persons demonstrated in Lyon at the call of the CGT, FSU, UNEF, CNT and SUD unions and the NPA, LFI and PCF political parties. They denounced acts of violence committed by members of far-right groups.
On 17 April 2023, several hundred nurses and other health workers gathered for a rally in Katowice, demanding higher wages and other social benefits.
On 8 September 2020, students and FGC activists gathered at the University Campus in Monserrato to protest against the limited enrolment established for health profession degrees.

On 23 June 2023, about 20 activists affiliated with Animal Rights protested in Gent (Vlaanderen), to demand that the owners of a slaughterhouse in Izegem, where Animal Rights members had shot footage of animal abuses, be convicted for animal abuse.

On 5 December 2019, on the day the government's deadline for voluntary evacuation of building occupations expired, more than 800 anarchists and members of anti-establishment groups marched in central Athens towards parliament shouting slogans against the evacuation of building occupations.

On 11 February 2023, around 80 people, including teachers, staged a protest march in Bailleul. The event was part of a fourth national and cross-sector day of strike and protest called by CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform.

On 14 November 2020, hundreds of citizens, including workers and employees of the hospitality industry, gathered in Andoain (Gipuzkoa) to protest against coronavirus restrictions in bars and restaurants. Protesters called on the government to provide greater financial support by decreasing taxation.

On 18 September 2021, demonstrators gathered in Dinan. They denounced coronavirus-related measures implemented by the government, including the bill on the obligation to provide the proof of the double vaccination to resume their professional and social activities.
On 4 November 2021, a group of activists of Arran burst into Endesa headquarters in Sabadell (Barcelona) to protest against the rise in electricity bills.
On 6 December 2022, farmers from Tromegja protested against the mass slaughter of pigs suspected of carrying the Western Nile Virus, and insist that they be tested before their slaughter.
On 4 February 2021, teachers and members of the SNES-FSU union demonstrated in front of the Porte Oceane high school in Le Havre. They denounced the suppression of teaching positions.

On 13 July 2024, thousands of LGBTQ+ community members and their supporters marched through Bristol (England) as part of the city's annual pride event, to celebrate the LGBTQIA+ community and campaign on banning conversion therapy and protecting the community's rights.
On 19 February 2023, local activists, joined by the Parbeszed vice-mayor of Budapest's 14th district, protested in Balatonfoldvar against the building of a pier in the lake of Balaton.

On 11 February 2023, around 400 people staged a protest march in Groix. The event was part of a fourth national and cross-sector day of strike and protest called by CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform.

On 10 November 2022, representatives from trade unions protested in Silistra to show their support for the protest of the Confederation of Independent Trade Unions in Bulgaria. The protests, which are taking place in several locations in Bulgaria, demand concrete assistance to workers to alleviate the ongoing economic crisis and inflation in the country, especially an increase to the minimum wage.

On 19 February 2025, around 150 people, including members of feminist groups, municipal opposition councilors, and PAH, held a protest outside the City Council in Santa Coloma de Gramenet (Cataluna) to protest against an event planned by Vox at the venue the following day. The protesters opposed Vox's use of the venue, given its stance against feminist spaces and gender equality policies. Although police officers formed a cordon and some protesters attempted to break through, the demonstration remained peaceful.

On 19 July 2023, residents of several villages along the Karlobat-Shumen road protested in Sungurlare due to way they claim is the terrible condition of the road, and they say that the many potholes cause flat tires, broken down cars, and that cars cannot move at more than 30 km per hour.

On 28 October 2023, during the afternoon, around 500 people gathered in the district St. Georg in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte for a spontaneous pro-Palestine demonstration. Clashes broke out with police officers who used tear gas. 2 police officers were injured.

On 8 May 2022, around 300 people with around 85 vehicles took part in a motorcade from Zweibrucken to Saarbrucken [coded to Saarbrucken] to protest against discrimination against Russian-speaking citizens amid the war in Ukraine, and to pay tribute to Soviet soldiers.

On 21 November 2024, farmers, including CR affiliates, gathered with a dozen tractors in Strasbourg (Grand Est), where they distributed 600 kilograms of apples in a demonstration. The event was part of a nationwide demonstration movement by French farmers opposing the EU-Mercosur trade deal and condemning delays in agricultural reforms promised by the previous government following the winter 2023-2024 farmers' demonstrations.
On 27 October 2018, 2018 in Croatia's capital Zagreb the Animal Liberation Initiative organized an international protest to ban hunting, attended by activists from several countries.
On 18 December 2020, Kurdish youth protested in Ludwigsburg for the release of PKK leader Abdullah Ocalan.

On 30 January 2023, people demonstrated in Parchim against coronavirus-related measures, inflation, and the threat of price increases on energy supplies. They also called for an end to the war in Ukraine and negotiations with Russia.
On 10 March 2022, HB activists held a protest in Valle de Trapaga-Trapagaran (Pais Vasco) to demand the independence of the Basque country and the amnesty of all convicted ETA armed group members.

On 11 March 2022, around 35 pro-Palestine campaigners belonging to Palestine Action holding placards and flags gathered outside Brighton Magistrates Court in Brighton to support their fellow activists standing trial for crimes allegedly committed at previous demonstrations.

On 8 February 2021, distributors linked with the hospitality industry drove around 200 vehicles in Lugo, demanding greater financial help. They protested over their difficult economic conditions caused by coronavirus restrictions in the service sector.
Around 2 February 2020 (as reported), farmers protested in Messkirch against the agrarian policy.

On 26 May 2024, at the call of a broad coalition, including The Greens, CSU, the Left and Ver.di, around 500 people, including local elected officials and parliamentarians, gathered in Lindenberg im Allgau (Bayern) to protest against the AfD.

On 24 October 2024, activists from the Grandparents' Climate Action (BKA) demonstrated in Askim, Viken, to urge stronger climate action, calling on politicians to take responsibility for future generations by intensifying efforts to combat climate change.
On 23 September 2022, people gathered for a protest organized by the Fridays for Future movement in front of the city hall in Chantilly, to advocate for action on the climate.

On 23 November 2022, students, mainly men, from Vauban gathered for a protest and left a banner reading 'In 24 feminicides it's the holidays,' in the cigarette corner of their Vauban high school courtyard in Brest, as a part of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, against violence done to women.

On 23 March 2023, hundreds of farmers and fishers, including the president of the Schleswig-Holstein Farmers' Association and members of the Schleswig-Holstein Poultry Association, demonstrated in Busum against the agricultural policy and financial cuts in crab fishing. They also were against the EU Commission's planned ban on bottom trawls in protected areas.
On 29 June 2020, around 50 left-wing activists protested in Innsbruck in front of a police station for the rights of refugees.

On 23 July 2022, demonstrators blocked access to the city hall in Bayonne at the call of the AP and Bake Bidea organizations. They called for the release of two elderly ETA Basque political prisoners and denounced their detention conditions for the last 32 years.

On 8 March 2022, kindergarten teachers protested in Cakovec against the Law on Preschool Education amendments, demanding better working conditions. These amendments imply that all teachers could work in kindergartens after minor training, which the kindergarten workers find degrading and discriminatory.

On 25 May 2024, at the call of SNES-FSU, SUD, CGT, FNEC FP-FO, CFDT, UNSA, and FCPE, people, including students' parents and teachers, gathered in Angers (Pays de la Loire) to express their opposition to the introduction of level groups for students.

On 24 December 2022, citizens engaged in a support march for the Ukrainian people in Cetinje. Citizens voiced the heroic resistance of the Ukrainian soldiers and citizens and condemned the violent Russian aggression.

On 18 May 2022, a group of teachers and workers gathered in front of the Isabella Gonzaga high school in Chieti (Chieti, Abruzzo), to ask for better working conditions for teachers and school employees who do not have the coronavirus 'green pass'.

On 28 October 2023, thousands of pro-Palestine protesters marched from Cavendish Road to Millennium Square in Leeds (England) to demand an end to the violence in Gaza. Protesters held signs reading 'freedom for Palestine'. West Yorkshire United for Palestine organized the protests.
On 3 November 2023, Fridays For Future activists demonstrated in Sundsvall, Vasternorrland, to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.

On 6 March 2021, between 400 and 500 persons demonstrated in Paimboeuf. They denounced the Carnet development project and its environmental consequences. Gendarmes officers were present but did not intervene.

On 24 August 2022, people marched in Copenhagen to show support and solidarity with the people of Ukraine as well as to mark the six-month anniversary of Russian invasion and Ukraine's Independence Day.
On 27 March 2024, an unknown number of people protested in Antwerpen (Vlaanderen) to demand the end of homelessness.
On 19 September 2022, people demonstrated in Greifswald against inflation.
On 18 February 2022, members and supporters of the SOR party protested in Floresti, against the increased gas prices, condemning the current PAS government.
Around 19 July 2020, (as reported) around 400 people protested in Rottenburg am Neckar for the preservation of a slaughterhouse at its current location.

On 7 June 2024, dozens of pro-Palestine activists held a protest in Sevilla (Andalucia), during a rugby match featuring the Israeli Elders of Zion team, demanding a free Palestine and condemning the Israeli military campaign in the Gaza Strip. One of the players punched a protester who was holding a Palestinian flag, before being expelled from the game.

On 26 July 2024, dozens of workers staged a protest in front of the entrance to the Costa Morena portal area in Brindisi (Puglia) against the lack of agreement on the revocation of the dismissal procedure for around 70 workers of the SIR company, and to ask their job retention, following the closure of the site. Protesters held two mannequins and a banner with the words 'Work and dignity'.
On 24 February 2022, a demonstration against the Russian invasion of Ukraine was held in Oulu.
On 24 September 2021, students affiliated with the FFF movement gathered for a rally in Leszno, demanding better protection of the climate.

On 5 December 2022, students at the Monti high school staged a demonstration in Chieri (Torino, Piemonte) to protest against cold classrooms due to the lack of heating and the conditions of the school building.
On 21 February 2020, residents of the Pissevin neighborhood gathered in Nimes. They protested against increased insecurity and recent gun shooting and drug trafficking in their neighborhood.

On 11 December 2024, public employees, called by CCOO, UGT, ANPE, USO, the Federation of Associations of Education Inspectors and Inspecting Officers (Federacion de Asociaciones de Inspectores e Inspectoras de Educacion - ADIDE), the Union of Education Inspectors (Union Sindical de Inspectores de Educacion - USIE), the Federal Police Union (Union Federal de Policia - UFP), ACAIP, and the Independent Union of the Tax Agency (Sindicato Independiente de la Agencia Tributaria - SIAT), held a protest outside Muface offices in Lugo (Galicia) to defend Muface, a mutual healthcare system, against potential integration into the public health system.
On 5 February 2021, Fridays For Future activists staged a protest in Kalmar to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.
On 1 April 2023, people, including Yellow Vests activists, took to the streets in Saint-Raphael against the pension reform bill.
On 1 August 2021, Pro Life activists gathered in Milano - Municipio 1 to protest against legal euthanasia. They claimed it is a form of 'legalized homicide'.

On 10 June 2020, people working in the arts sector gathered in front of Michetti Theatre in Pescara to protest against their current condition. In fact they can't work due to the measures imposed to avoid the spread of coronavirus.

On 5 December 2020, about 500 people, most of them students from the Toscana region and their parents, gathered in Duomo square in Florence (Firenze, Toscana) to protest against the delay in the reopening of schools announced by a government decree to manage the coronavirus emergency and denounce the lack of government's proposals regarding the transport of students in compliance with coronavirus security measures. The protest was part of a national protest movement organized by Priority to School, with similar demonstrations occurring across Italy on that day.

On 22 November 2022, about 60 magistrates, clerks, lawyers, and judicial assistants gathered in front of the courtroom of the judicial court of Grenoble to denounce their working conditions. The event was part of a national strike day called by USM and SM, as well as other unions, to denounce a lack of resources and staff in the sector.

On 4 April 2025, people, called by CSIF, gathered outside the government sub-delegation in Salamanca (Castilla y Leon) to protest in defense of public sector working conditions. Demonstrators denounced delayed salary increases, loss of purchasing power, and the lack of implementation of a 0.5 percent wage adjustment agreed in 2022. Participants also called for improved retirement provisions and early retirement mechanisms for civil servants.

On 28 March 2023, between 260 (according to the police) and 300 (unions) demonstrators took to the streets in Elbeuf. The event was part of a tenth national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FIDL, FAGE, and MNL) to oppose the passing of a pension reform bill by means of Article 49.3 of the constitution by the government, and call for the withdrawal of the bill.

On 2 July 2022, at the call of MFPF, around 50 people, including women and members of the PCF and Attac, gathered in Marseille. They called for the fundamental right to abortion for women after the US Supreme Court decided to revoke it.

On 2 June 2020, a protest organized by right and center-right wing parties Lega, Forward Italy and Brothers of Italy to protest against the current Italian coalition government and its management of the coronavirus emergency took place in Cesenatico (Forli-Cesena, Emilia-Romagna). More than 100 people participated, including supporters, activists and local administrators.

Around 23 July 2021 (as reported), over 500 people took the street in Palermo (Palermo, Sicilia) to pay tribute to an anti-mafia magistrate killed in the 1992 Via D'Amelio bombing and protest against mafia presence within the state.

On 24 June 2021, Extinction Rebellion activists staged a protest performance in Stockholm to oppose one of the Swedish oil and gas exploration and production companies that funds exploration projects in the Arctic region.
On 7 November 2021, approximately 100 local residents protested in Lokva Rogoznica, Croatia, after the owner of a hotel illegally blocked off car access to the coast.
On 3 September 2024, at the call of FISASCAT CISL and FILCAMS CGIL, Brindisi Multiservizi workers demonstrated in Brindisi (Puglia) to demand answers and security for the workers' future.

On 15 February 2024, about 200 members of the anti-establishment sector marched in central Thessaloniki against the police and the arrest of rioters in the earlier demonstration against the establishment of private universities in the country. A group of rioters hurled rocks and threw flares from the rooftop of a university building at the riot police forces down below. Police responded with stun grenades.
On 8 September 2020, people protested in Ruse demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Borisov and chief prosecutor Geshev over alleged corruption and links to mafia.

On 25 November 2021, during the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, around 2000 people gathered in Granada (Andalucia) to protest against gender-based violence. The 8M and 25N platforms were involved in the protest.
On 16 January 2021, employees from dance schools across the country protested in Sofia against the coronavirus measures that prevent them from working.

On 25 January 2022, around 350 climate activists camped and demonstrated in Osterholz to call for the preservation of the forest as well as an end to the ongoing evacuation of the camp. Police officers tried to evacuate the camp. Around 1,500 trees are to be felled to make way for a spoil heap of the lime industry.

On 16 February 2023, 650 people gathered for a protest in Langres. The event was part of a fifth national and cross-sector day of strike and protest called by the CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform.

On 1 March 2021, environmentalists protested in Plovdiv against the destruction of nature on the Black Sea Coast, demanding a ban on construction and proclaiming the sand dunes in Kamchiyski Pyasatsi a protected area.

On 9 September 2020, around 1,000 people protested in Kiel for the reception of refugees from the Greek refugee camp Moria in which a fire had broken out the previous night. The protest was organised by Seebruecke.
On 30 January 2022, citizens protested in Villalbilla (Madrid) against the presence of a man who was previously accused of sexual abuse of children in a municipality 30km close to Villalbilla.

On 21 January 2018, far right rioters heading to the rally in central Thessaloniki against the use of the name Macedonia by the neighbouring Former Yugoslav Republic clashed with members of the free social space 'The School', who are occupying an old school building. The rioters attacked the building using stones and teargas. No injuries were reported.
On 9 March 2023, raspberry farmers blocked the road in Bijelo Polje, demanding state subventions to continue their work.

On 26 February 2024, farmers and supporters staged a protest in Frankfurt (Oder) (Brandenburg), blocking the city bridge with some vehicles and causing traffic disruptions. The protest aimed to address agricultural concerns and was part of a nationwide demonstration movement against the federal coalition government and its agricultural policies.

On 27 February 2025, at around 6:25 pm, around 100 people gathered in Berlin - Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf (Berlin) to demonstrate against an event featuring Austrian far-right figure and Identitarian Movement Austria (IBOE) member Martin Sellner. The demonstration first took place outside the restaurant where the event was taking place on Uhlandstrasse, before moving towards Bundesallee. Shortly before the police arrived, a participant sprayed pepper spray into the restaurant, causing eye irritation to at least one event attendee. Demonstrators later attempted to obstruct attendees from leaving the venue but eventually dispersed following verbal warnings by the police. The demonstration concluded shortly after 9:00 pm, with five demonstrators remaining. Authorities launched an investigation into the pepper spray incident as a case of dangerous bodily harm.

On 10 July 2022, people gathered outside the Prefecture in Genova to show their support for the Chief prosecutor of Catanzaro, who was threatened by the mafia. The Agende Rosse Movement organized the demonstration. A FdI council member took part in the event.

On 30 March 2024, residents of Novi Beograd and activists marched and blocked the road in Belgrade - Novi Beograd, voicing their dissatisfaction with the local government's plans to build a skyscraper within the green areas of this part of the city.

On 14 July 2022, drivers of vehicles for hire (VTC) demonstrated in Saint-Tropez. They denounced municipal restrictions on access to the port, denouncing the consequences on their professional activity.

On 23 October 2021, around 2000 members of the law enforcement authorities protested in Barcelona, demanding respect for their work. They complained about being subjected to constant direct attacks. The Police Union of Catalonia (SPC) and the Independent Union of the Mossos (USPAC) were involved in the protest.
On 18 October 2022, around 100 bakers staged a protest outside the cabinet of the Wallonian Minister of Economy in Namur to demand governmental support for their rising energy costs.

On 28 September 2023, Unemployed '7 November' activists symbolically occupied the 'Maschio Angioino' medieval castle in Napoli (Campania, Napoli) to protest against the lack of job opportunities and training courses and demanded a meeting with the municipal authorities.
On 1 May 2023, at the call of SPOE and SJOE, people gathered at Marktplatz in Schwertberg, to protest for workers rights on the occasion of International Worker's Day.

On 26 January 2025, following leaked cell phone calls of the last moments of the victims of the Tempe rail disaster, protesters rallied in Spetses at the call of the association of the victims' families. The protesters demanded justice and accused the government of a cover-up. This was part of a large mobilization in more than 150 nationwide and international locations with the slogan 'I Have No Oxygen', the last words of one of the victims.
On 1 February 2022, teachers and students gathered in Aubin to denounce the suppression of the masonry branch at the High School of Wood and Housing Professions of Aubin.
On 9 October 2020, protesters gathered in Jesi (Ancona, Marche) on the occasion of the Sixth Global Climate Strike organized by the Fridays for Future movement.
On 15 July 2020, residents of Cowdenbeath, Fife, rioted in front of an alleged paedophile's home, which escalated as rioters threw things at the attending police.

On 13 February 2020, an unspecified number of people, among which metalworkers affiliated with CISL, UIL and CGIL, took part in a sit-in in Palazzo square in Torino to raise awareness of the crisis faced by metalworkers in Piemonte.

On 25 May 2021, a group of people staged a protest at the Plein in Den Haag to denounce the coronavirus policy of the Dutch government. As the protest wasn't authorized, police forces intervened and arrested a large part of the protesters.
On 11 March 2023, automotive workers, called by CCOO and UGT, held a protest in Malaga (Andalucia) demanding higher salaries.

On 2 September 2023, demonstrators, including members of the Russian community, protested in Oslo against Swiss-Norwegian shipping company that continues to transport Russian oil, among others things.

On 26 September 2024, at the end of a march in central Thessaloniki, demanding justice for the Pakistani national who died in police custody in the Agios Panteleimon precinct in Athens, his body bearing obvious marks of beatings, a group of demonstrators hurled rocks at riot police, who responded with tear gas and stun grenades.
On 5 April 2024, Women's Strike movement activists demonstrated in Stockholm in support of women's rights and to oppose violence against women.

On 15 September 2023, ethnic Serbs affiliated with SNSD protested in Foca against the prosecution of Milorad Dodik, the SNSD leader currently under prosecution for jeopardizing the Dayton Peace Accords and the failure to implement the decisions of the High Representative to Bosnia and Herzegovina, Christian Schmidt.

On 27 April 2024, hundreds of XR activists chained themselves and some of them occupied the entrance of the Intesa Sanpaolo bank in Torino (Piemonte) to protest against the G7 Environment Summit that will take place in the coming days. Protesters held banners with the words 'Climate crisis: deciding together' and 'Seven governments decide, the whole world burns'.

On 16 November 2023, around 200 people protested in Eindhoven Central Station (Noord-Brabant), calling for a ceasefire in Gaza and expressing solidarity with the Palestinian population. The protesters chanted the slogan 'from the river to the sea, Palestine will be free' and condemned the Dutch government for supporting the Israeli government.

On 24 January 2021, around 20 members of the political party RN from all over the region protested in Pau against migration and a national plan for the reception of asylum seekers and the integration of refugees.

On 19 April 2024, three activists from Extinction Rebellion attempted to disrupt the departure of an international flight in Lappeenranta, Etela-Karjala, calling for a complete end to subsidies and tax breaks for the aviation industry. The activists were later escorted out by police without the use of force.

On 11 July 2020, people gathered in Cesenatico (Forli-Cesena, Emilia-Romagna) under the banner 'Let's Remain Free' to protest against a draft law against homotransphobia. Protesters claimed that such a law would affect their freedom of expression, education, religion, social and political aggregation.

On 8 October 2022, members of AnimaNaturalis and CAS International held a protest in Logrono (La Rioja) to demand equal protection before the law for dogs used in hunting activities, whether sports or hunting, criticizing the recent amendment, which they claimed would exclude dogs used in hunting from the next Law of Protection and Rights for Animals.

On 13 February 2022, citizens called by 'We are not crime platform' protested in Vitoria-Gasteiz, demanding the repeal of the Law on Public Safety. They said that the law limits freedoms and criminalises protest activity. The CNT, CGT, Amnesty International, Ecologists in Action, Greenpeace and CEAR unions and organizations were involved in the demonstration.
On 11 May 2021, cleaning and domestic sector workers, predominantly women, including CCOO and UGT union members, protested in Albacete over precarious working conditions.

On 25 November 2021, in the morning, around 300 people, including Non Una di Meno activists, marched from Roma square to Dante square in Catania (Catania, Sicilia) to denounce gender-based violence, specifically against women. The event was organized on the occasion of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.

On 5 November 2021, around 500 people, including former workers of Whirlpool's Neapolitan plant, S.I. COBAS affiliates, road maintenance workers and unoccupied people, some of them affiliated with the local '7 November' and 'New Benches' movements, gathered outside the Prefecture, in Plebiscito square, in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to demand answers regarding their professional future and ask to meet with the Labor Minister, visiting the city's mayor on that day. At least one umbrella was thrown at a police cordon standing outside the Prefecture, generating tension.

On 17 April 2021, around 20 anti-government protesters including supporters of the Socialist Workers Party and ACORN marched in the Regent Circus area of Swindon in a show of opposition against the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Bill which proposes to give police more powers to shutdown peaceful protests.

On 19 March 2025, overnight, unidentified individuals set fire to a van parked in front of a police station in Stuttgart (Baden-Wuerttemberg) in a symbolic act of solidarity with political prisoners, particularly antifascists and leftists. A statement claiming responsibility, published on the Indymedia platform, described the arson as a response to state repression, including public manhunts, house searches, long prison sentences, and the criminalization of left-wing activism. The statement also called for continued militant politics by women against patriarchy, war, fascism, and in support of the class struggle.

On 27 March 2021, around 200 cars participated in a vehicular protest through Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, demanding a change to the city electoral system after a popular mayoral candidate dropped out of the race.

On 24 October 2020, people gathered in Mont-de-Marsan, at the call of unions (UNSA, CGT, FCPE, SUD), the MRAP, LDH, La Cimade, PCF, Generation.s, Amnesty International, Muslim organizations, and MP. They demonstrated as part of a national tribute to a teacher, deadly attacked days before. They also demonstrated for freedom of speech.

On 1 May 2025, people participated in a protest organized by the Socialist Party and the National Congress of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs, marching from the Circus to the Opera and Ballet Theatre in Chisinau - Buiucani. The demonstration was directed against the PAS leadership and the president, calling for social justice and dialogue with Russia. The protest was led by Socialist Party members of Parliament. There are indications that participants were brought to the event via organized transportation. The Soviet song 'Katyusha' was played during the event.

On 8 May 2023, citizens, teachers and civil society representatives marched through Kragujevac in a 'Serbia against violence', triggered by mass murder events in a primary school in Belgrade and a village in Mladenovac. Citizens blame the violence-contaminated public discourse, from praising former war criminals by high-level politicians to tv-shows on national frequencies filled with inappropriate content. Citizens also called on the government to take responsibility for such a situation.

On 1 April 2023, 40 anarchist activists took to the streets of Cesena (Emilia-Romagna, Forli-Cesena) to demonstrate in solidarity with Alfredo Cospito, a well-known anarchist currently on hunger strike to demonstrate against the 41-bis prison regime, and 3 other anarchists currently charged with theft, among others, after a 'No Green Pass' demonstration held on 13 November 2021.

On 25 November 2020, at the call of Reseau feministe 37, around 100 people, including Osez le feminisme 37 (Dare Feminism), NT 37, the education branch of SUD 37, MFPF 37, and CGT 37, gathered in Tours. They denounced violence against women on the occasion of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.

On 18 July 2022, people demonstrated in Geislingen (Zollernalbkreis) against the war in Ukraine and a possible world war, imperialism (led by Russia, EU, and NATO), as well as to denounce the governments' poverty policy. Demonstrators denounced inflation and called for a significant wage increase for all. They also called for more climate protection (coal-phase out).
On 10 January 2024, farmers gathered for a rally in Dachsenhausen (Rhein-Lahn-Kreis). The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement against planned agricultural subsidy cuts.

On 11 April 2023, striking NHS junior doctors represented by BMA formed a picket line outside Addenbrooke's Hospital in Cambridge over a pay dispute and working conditions. The event was part of a four-day national industrial action.

On 31 May 2020, Extinction Rebellion activists staged a socially-distanced demonstration outside of the castle in Colchester near High Street, calling for a Citizens Assembly to determine how to move forward from the coronavirus pandemic.

On 9 April 2024, people demonstrated outside of the Norwegian Environment Agency' office in Helsfyr, Oslo, against plans for disposing construction waste in the Oslo Fjord linked to the development of a new port in Fredrikstad. Police personnel were present but did not intervene.

On 9 March 2025, citizens blocked the main road connecting Belgrade and Kragujevac in Topola for one hour to support students and striking teachers who are demanding accountability for the 15 lives lost in the collapse of a concrete canopy at the train station in Novi Sad. The protest began with a 15-minute moment of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stops' campaign to honor the victims and emphasize their demands.

On 21 October 2020, in the afternoon, cleaning staff and multi-utility companies' employees staged a protest in Bari (Bari, Puglia) to demand the renewal of their national labor contract and better contract conditions. Protesters gathered at the call of trade unions FILCAMS CGIL, FISASCAT CISL and UIL Transport.

On 1 May 2023, at the call of CGIL, CISL, and UIL, thousands of people took to the streets in Parma (Emilia-Romagna), from D'Azeglio street to Garibaldi square, on the occasion of Labor Day, to demand better working conditions and increased safety at work. The city's mayor (IiC) took part in the demonstration.

On 27 January 2022, between 300 and 350 people, including teachers, health workers and LO activists, demonstrated in Sete, at the call of 4 interprofessional unions (CGT, FO, Sud, FSU) and 4 student groups (FIDL, MNL, UNEF, VL). They called for an increase in salaries and improved purchasing power.

On 4 September 2018, 2018 in Belgrade settlement of Vozdovac, parents of children attending elementary school 'Zmaj Jovan Jovanovic' staged a protest over frequent changes of teachers in their children's class.
On 12 May 2023, Fridays For Future activists demonstrated in Vasteras, Vastmanland, to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.

On 15 June 2024, 80 people demonstrated in Montluel (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to demand a ceasefire in Gaza, express solidarity with the Palestinian people, and condemn what they deemed a 'genocide' of Gazans by the Israeli army.

On 19 October 2020, around 100 persons, including the mayor of the city, gathered in front of the city hall in Montargis. They observed a minute of silence as part of a national tribute to a teacher, deadly attacked days before. They also demonstrated for freedom of speech.

On 25 May 2024, farmers protested in Strumica, demanding that the buying price of tomatoes be increased, claiming that the low prices does not even cover the price of production and stimulates overconsumption, and that they can't keep up with demand.
On 25 May 2022, an unknown number of Black Lives Matter demonstrators gathered for a protest in London - Haringey, against systemic racism, and in remembrance of George Floyd.

On 22 October 2018, citizens in Bosnian northwestern city of Bihac continued their protest against the situation with migrants in their city. Residents are concerned over the number of migrants in the city, as well as the location and conditions of the facilities in which they are accommodated, and increased crime rates in the city.
On 5 June 2020, Revival organized a protest outside the U.S. Embassy in Sofia in support of U.S. President Donald Trump and against what they termed 'the terror' by Black Lives Matter protesters.
On 1 November 2023, people demonstrated in Tranemo, Vastra Gotaland, against budget cuts in the education sector.

On 16 March 2023, an unknown number of people assembled in Calais to block the access to the port to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution. The evet was called by CGT.
On 17 July 2020, Fridays For Future activists staged a protest in front of the City Hall in Umea to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.
On 8 May 2020, about 50 people protested in Straubing. The exact reason for the protest was not reported, but it is likely in connection with the coronavirus lockdown measures.
On 5 November 2021, about 100 students affiliated with the FFF movement gathered for a rally in Katowice, demanding better protection of the climate.

On 26 May 2021, CGIL, CISL and UIL trade union affiliates and supporters gathered outside the Lombardia Region headquarters (Palazzo Lombardia) in Milano - Municipio 9 (Milano, Lombardia) to protest against work-related deaths and demand more safety guarantees for workers. The event was part of a national week of protest organized by CGIL, CISL and UIL and called 'No more deaths at work'.

On 14 November 2022, activists from Extinction Rebellion staged a protest outside of a branch of Barclays bank at Clapham junction in London - Wandsworth, calling for the bank to end its investment in the fossil fuel industry. This event was part of the national day of action against Barclays bank.
On 10 March 2022, people gathered in Kungsangen to denounce the Russian invasion of Ukraine and call on authorities to promote peace. The event was organized by Upplands-Bro Municipality.

On 16 June 2024, about 30 people, including Ukrainian citizens (mostly Ukrainian women), protested against the public screening in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) of the pro-Russia movie 'The Witness', whose production was financed by the Government of the Russian Federation. Protesters displayed Ukrainian national flags, sang the national anthem, and criticized the Russian Federation government and president.

On 31 May 2023, around 30 people, including union affiliates, assembled in front of the Fulbert high school in Chartres, where Renaissance and LR MPs were visiting the school, to denounce the pension reform of the government and demand its withdrawal. Police forces pushed back some protesters who attempted to enter the school's parking lot.

On 13 January 2024, several hundred people, including Palestinian ambassador Salah Abdel Shafi, participated in a pro-Palestine protest in Vienna - Inner City (Wien 1-Innere Stadt) to call for an immediate and permanent ceasefire.

On 6 February 2025, in the morning, at the call of trade unions CGT, CFDT, FO, and SUD, between 300 and 500 people gathered in front of the regional council at Porte d'Aix in Marseille (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to protest against a 31% reduction in subsidies allocated to professional integration centers (missions locales). The protesters, including employees of the centers, young people, and former beneficiaries, expressed concern over the negative impact of this funding cut, emphasizing that it would hinder their efforts to support vulnerable young people aged 16 to 25 in overcoming employment and social obstacles.

On 11 April 2023, health workers held a protest in Lugo (Lugo, Galicia) to demand a better organization of the service and better conditions for doctors who are suffering from a lack of personnel. The protest and indefinite strike was summoned by CESM.
On 19 April 2021, Sir workers gathered at the Costa Morena Est customs passage in Brindisi to protest against the cut in salaries for 38 workers. The labor union UIL supported the demonstration.

On 2 April 2025, protests against violence against children and paedophilia took place in Plovdiv, provoked by the widespread discontent in the country over what they claim are the increasing cases of child abuse after five men were arrested for sexually exploiting children between the ages of two months and 14 years online.

On 13 November 2021, around 30 students occupied an administrative building of the Paris-Nanterre university in Paris. They demanded the enrollment of 61 students who remained without assigned course at the start of the school year.
On 5 December 2023, at the call of STC, around 100 municipal workers gathered in Ajaccio (Corse) to demand a pay rise.

On 3 February 2025, at the national call of Slc CGIL, Fistel CISL, and Uilcom UIL, call center workers gathered in Citta di Lombardia Square and in Testi Street in Milano - Municipio 9 (Lombardia) to demonstrate against several companies potentially withdrawing from the national collective labor agreement for the telecommunications sector in favor of a new contract that, according to demonstrators, worsens working conditions by reducing sick pay and paid leave while also eliminating seniority-based pay increases.

On 22 June 2024, at the call of CNT, striking Acqua hotel maids - most of them women - gathered for a picket line outside the Radisson hotel in Marseille (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to demand a pay rise.

On 14 July 2021, residents of the 37th Block protested and briefly blocked traffic with their bodies in their neighborhood in Belgrade - Novi Beograd, Serbia, against construction of a multi-story building where a park now is.

On 17 June 2020, demonstrators gathered in front of the IEF factory in Montreuil, including members of Attac, Extinction Rebellion and Yellow Vests. They protested, as part of a day of actions to 'refuse the re-intoxication of the world', against a de-pollution and redevelopment project due to be carried out on the site.

On 19 February 2025, in the afternoon, several dozen people marched from the train station to the courthouse in Tours (Centre-Val de Loire) to protest against the release from custody of a motorist who ran over and killed a 30-year-old Congolese student on 15 February 2025. They demanded justice for the victim.

On 28 March 2023, between 10,000 (according to the police) and 20,000 (unions) people took to the streets of Montpellier to demonstrate. The event was part of a tenth national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FAGE, FIDL, and MNL) to oppose the passing of a pension reform bill by means of Article 49.3 of the constitution by the government, and call for the withdrawal of the bill.

On 10 October 2021, people, among them CGIL members, gathered in Reggio Emilia (Reggio nell'Emilia, Emilia-Romagna) to guard the CGIL branch in protest against the far-right assault on the union's headquarters in Rome. The Mayor of Reggio Emilia, a PD MP, Legacoop, and a regional council member took part in the event.

On 27 June 2019, a group of 12 citizens from Dubrovnik, Croatia started a 529-kilometer-long peace march to Srebrenica, Bosnia and Herzegovina to commemorate all civilian victims of the war in Bosnia.

On 10 February 2022, in the evening, three municipal officials gathered in downtown Manfredonia (Foggia, Puglia) to protest against the increase in commodity prices. The event was part of a national evening of protest, by which municipalities briefly turned off the light of their landmarks' facades, organized by ANCI.

On 24 February 2023, in the morning, ALG activists blocked traffic on Schuttelstrasse near Praterstern in Vienna - Leopoldstadt, gluing themselves to the tarmac, to call for more climate action. The participants were removed from the street by the police. Other simultaneous road blockades were staged by the environmental group in other parts of Vienna [coded as separate events], resulting in a total of 23 arrests. The actions were supported by Seniors for Future and Parents for Future.

On 12 July 2023, around 70 farmers, summoned by UPA and COAG, held a protest in Villardeciervos (Zamora, Castilla y Leon) to demand compensation for the fires in the Sierra de la Culebra, which occurred a year ago.
On 30 October 2020, activists, mostly women, gathered for a rally in Przeworsk protesting against restrictions of abortions in Poland. The event was coordinated by the Women's Strike.

On 20 April 2024, around 25 Last Generation activists gathered in Saarbrucken (Saarland), demanding increased government action on climate change, resulting in 6 participants being taken into custody by the police.

On 26 March 2021, students, parents, teachers and school personnel gathered in L'Aquila (L'Aquila, Abruzzo) to protest against the recent reintroduction of distance learning amidst rising coronavirus infections concerns and demand the reopening of schools with sufficient security guarantees and greater public investments. The event was part of a day of protest called jointly by the Priority to School committee and the COBAS trade union.

On 10 February 2022, several members and supporters of the SOR party, including a SOR mayor, protested near the president's residence in Condrita, condemning the failing repurposing of the Condrita residence into a domestic violence shelter.

On 14 March 2023, nearly 30 teachers of the Joseph-Saverne high school, including SNES-FSU affiliates, demonstrated in front of their institute in Isle-Jourdain, to denounce the decrease in resources allocated by the National Education for the start of the 2023 school year.
On 27 March 2021, a vehicular protest for 'an independent Montenegro' was held Bijelo Polje, Montenegro. The participants accused the government of loyalism to Serbia.

On 11 March 2024, farmers protested in Gijon (Asturias), blocking the port of Musel. The event was part of a nationwide farmers' demonstration movement against the ratification of the EU's free-trade agreements until partner third countries comply with the EU's agricultural standards, and in favor of fair production prices for Spanish farmers, relief measures to offset the consequences of droughts and the import of agricultural products from Ukraine, as well as better working and social conditions in their sector.

On 26 August 2023, people, called by the Platform in Defense of a Decent Health of the Basic Health Zone of Tabara, staged a massive protest in Tabara (Zamora, Castilla y Leon) demanding better health care services, including employing more health care professionals so that the health centers operate 24/7 and offer specialist patient care.
On 13 November 2021, people demonstrated in Sonderborg to oppose the repatriation of Syrian refugees as some parts of Syria are now considered safe by the Danish government.
On 10 May 2020, a dozen merchants staged a protest in Marcinelle against the persistent ban on market activities due to the coronavirus measures.

On 23 March 2021, workers from a wide range of categories gathered, at the call of CGIL, CISL and UIL, in Terni (Terni, Umbria) to call for concrete help measures and for a better acknowledgment of their categories from the Umbria regional government amidst the coronavirus emergency.
On 19 December 2021, activists gathered for a rally in Zory, protesting against a new law on media ownership, which they perceive as a harmful pressure of the government against independent media.

On 24 June 2023, 56,000 people, according to the prefecture, took to the streets of Paris (Ile-de-France), as part of a pride march to defend the right of their community and against homophobic and transphobic acts.
On 22 October 2021, dozens of citizens protested in Salamanca (Castilla y Leon), demanding better railroad networks.

On 24 October 2021, 28 people protested in front of the Ministry of Sport (BMKOS) in Vienna - Inner City to call for a diplomatic boycott of the 2022 Beijing Olympics, citing the 'genocide' of Uyghurs by China.

On 16 August 2020, an unknown number of people protested in Kapu, against the 'destruction' of forests in Estonia and 'demanded change' from the Estonian government on this topic. The protest was part of an all-Estonia rally, which took place in at least 22 locations across the country.

On 19 January 2023, around 1,550 people staged a protest in Maubeuge. The event was part of a national and cross-sector day of strike and protest called by CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform.

On 13 January 2020, early in the morning over five hundred people gathered in Quarto to demonstrate against the installation of a 5G antenna. During the demonstration some tensions rose and a clash occurred between the police and the demonstrators. No injuries were reported.

On 13 December 2024, at the call of CGT and UNSA, around 40 striking municipal workers gathered outside the town hall in Chantepie (Bretagne) to protest against the introduction of a minimum service provision (SMA) during strikes. The protesters argued that this measure, allowing authorities to compel certain workers to remain on duty, undermined their right to strike.

On 2 May 2024, a group of activists gathered for a rally in Prague near the Faculty of Humanities, declaring their support to civilians in Gaza and condemning the violence perpetrated by Israel. They also criticized what they see as pro-Israeli orientation of the university and demanded a dismissal of the leading expert on Israeli affairs over her alleged strong pro-Israel bias. The activists claimed being affiliated to the academic community, but the faculty dean questioned their affiliation.
On 20 November 2020, people held a car procession in front of the Presidential residence in Sofia, demanding the resignation of the government cabinet.

On 30 November 2023, at the call of the Peace Palestine Collective (Collectif Paix Palestine), around 30 people gathered outside the train station in Saint-Brieuc (Bretagne) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people in Gaza.

On 15 October 2022, members of AKEL and its affiliated union PEO held a demonstration march over the cost of living crisis and accused the government of depriving workers of 7.5 billion euros worth of income during ten years in office. The demonstrators marched from the finance ministry to the presidential palace in Nicosia where they handed a memo to the director of the president's press office.

On 28 March 2023, 300 (according to the unions) demonstrators took to the streets in Gisors. The event was part of a tenth national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FIDL, FAGE, and MNL) to oppose the passing of a pension reform bill by means of Article 49.3 of the constitution by the government, and call for the withdrawal of the bill.

On 22 October 2021, between 200 and 300 people from across Friuli-Venezia Giulia and Lombardia gathered in Unita square in Trieste (Trieste, Friuli-Venezia Giulia), some holding flowers to symbolize the gathering's peacefulness, to protest against the extension of coronavirus 'green pass' restrictions to public and private sector workers in their workplace, which came into effect on 15 October 2021, and express solidarity with Trieste workers striking against the measure. Some protesters who had occupied the square overnight were cleared by police, although no violent interaction was reported.

On 7 September 2024, 1,000 people, including a national deputy (LFI), demonstrated from the train station to the main market square in Angouleme (Nouvelle-Aquitaine). The event was part of a national demonstration called by USL, Ue, LFI, Attac, NT, PCF, LE, NPA, Generation.s, Pd!, The Aftermath, and MFPF against French President Emmanuel Macron's decision to appoint Michel Barnier (an LR affiliate) as Prime Minister rather than one of the names suggested by NFP, the left-wing coalition that won the most votes in the June and July 2024 parliamentary elections, denouncing an 'autocratic' shift.

On 5 September 2021, an unknown number of workers from the cultural sector protested at the Formula 1 race track in Zandvoort (Noord-Holland) to demand more attention for the cultural sector in the context of the coronavirus measures of the Dutch government.

On 16 September 2020, a dozen private health workers gathered with banners in front of the Confindustria offices in Bologna to protest against the non-renewal of their national contract. The demonstration was organized by the Labor Unions CGIL, CISL and UIL.

On 8 February 2024, activists gathered for a rally in Lucenec, protesting against what they see as anti-democratic interference with the state institutions, especially the prosecutors' agencies and the judiciary.

On 25 March 2022, in the morning, as part of the Global Climate Strike called by FFF, students, FFF, Legambiente and other local environmental activists took to the streets in Ravenna (Ravenna, Emilia-Romagna) to demand more climate action.
Around 21 May 2022, RFSU activists demonstrated in Kungsbacka to draw attention to the issue of infant mortality and in support of reproductive rights.

On 7 March 2023, an unknown number of people staged a protest in Caen. The event was part of a sixth national and cross-sector day of strike and protest called by unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and students' organizations to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform.
On 24 October 2020, several hundred activists, mostly women, gathered for a rally in Warsaw, protesting against restrictions of abortions in Poland. The event was coordinated by the Women's Strike.

On 14 September 2024, around 2,500 people participated in the Christopher Street Day (CSD) parade in Dortmund (Nordrhein-Westfalen), to protest for LGBTQ+ rights and visibility. Around 50 right-wing individuals staged a counter-protest nearby, while at the call of Antifa, around 150 left-wing protesters demonstrated against the right-wing protest. The police effectively kept the groups apart. Two right-wing protesters were detained for making homophobic remarks and performing a Hitler salute. In addition, there were minor incidents, including children attempting to throw eggs at CSD participants.

On 29 June 2023, overnight, rioters vandalized several shops including a hair salon in Joigny. The event was part of a national wave of riots and demonstrations denouncing police violence and demanding justice in the wake of the shooting and subsequent death of 17-year-old Nahel M. by a police officer in Nanterre on 27 June 2023.
On 15 February 2023, around 100 unionized workers protested outside a factory in Fagaras, demanding that the previous director be reinstated.

On 24 April 2024, protesters gathered in front of the Ministry of Internal Affairs building in Sofia due to the arrest of journalist Dimitar Stoyanov from Bird BG on what they claim are trumped-up charges of hooliganism and weapons possession. The protest was organized by the BOEC association.
